additionalPlain:
Who We Are

Loft Orbital builds “shareable” satellites, providing a fast & simple path to orbit for organizations that require access to space. Powered by our hardware & software products, we operate satellites, fly customer payloads onboard, and handle entire missions from end to end - significantly reducing the lead-time and risk of a traditional space mission.

Our standard interface enables us to fly multiple customer payloads on the same satellite, with capabilities such as earth imagery, weather & climate /science data collection, IoT connectivity, in-orbit demonstrations, and national security missions. Our customers trust us to manage their space infrastructure, so they can focus on what matters most to them: operating their mission and collecting their data.

At Loft, you’ll be given the autonomy and ownership to solve significant challenges, but with a close-knit and supportive team at your back. We believe that diversity and community are the foundation of an open culture. We are committed to hiring the best people regardless of background and make their time at Loft the most fulfilling period of their career.

We value kind, supportive and team-oriented collaborators. It is also crucial for us that you are a problem solver and a great communicator. As our team is international, you will need strong English skills to better collaborate, easily communicate complex ideas and convey important messages.

With 3 satellites on-orbit and a wave of exciting missions launching soon, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France.

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.


 *Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Loft, we value respectful debate and people who aren’t afraid to challenge assumptions.  We strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check all the boxes.

Who We Are

Loft: Space Made Simple. 

Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.

description:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
Loft Orbital is looking for a Cash Analyst to join our Finance team and support the cash management of our growing international business.

In this role, you’ll work closely with our Finance and Accounting teams across the US and France on daily cash positioning, weekly cash reporting and cash forecasting. You’ll get direct visibility into the numbers behind a fast-growing, international space company.

This is a great opportunity for someone with first time experience in Finance who enjoys working with numbers, pays close attention to detail, and wants to take on more ownership over time.

lists.content:
• Track customer receipts and supplier payments against forecast, and flag timing risks early.
  • Monitor daily cash positions across Loft’s bank accounts, legal entities and currencies.
  • Prepare weekly cash reporting, including the weekly cash update to the founders and the 13-week cash forecast.
  • Take progressive ownership of the 13-week cash forecast, keeping it current with actuals and inputs from Accounting, FP&A and program teams.
  • Support, and progressively own, the analysis of cash burn, runway and cash scenarios (e.g. delayed collections, hiring or capex changes).
  • Analyze forecast-to-actual cash variances and use the findings to improve forecast accuracy.
  • Support annual and multi-year cash projections with FP&A.
  • Work closely with Accounting and FP&A to ensure consistent methodologies and timely delivery of consolidated reporting.
  • Build strong, trusted relationships across the company (programs, Opex owners, leadership) and help position Finance as a key business partner.
  • Support the optimization and automation of cash management tools and processes, with increasing use of AI.
  • Work with distributed teams across the US and France.

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 1–3 years of relevant experience in Finance, Accounting, Treasury, Audit, or a related analytical role.
  • High Excel proficiency.
  • Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy with financial data.
  • Curious, analytical mindset, with a willingness to understand the “why” behind the numbers.
  • Proactive, with the ability to take initiative and propose improvements to processes and tools.
  • Ability to deliver on time and work autonomously, sometimes under tight deadlines.
  • Team player with a collaborative mindset, comfortable working across teams and time zones.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Hands-on experience with Claude is a plus.
  • Industry background in a project-based or industrial environment (aerospace is a plus).
  • Exposure to bank reconciliations, payment processing, Accounts Payable, or Accounts Receivable.
  • Experience with an ERP, NetSuite preferred.
  • Experience supporting an international or multi-entity organization.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks in office
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for birthing parent and 10 weeks for non-birthing parent
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

salaryDescription: State law requires us to tell you the base compensation range for this role, which is $105,000 - $125,000 per year, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.  The salary range for this role is intentionally wide as we evaluate individuals based on their unique experience and abilities to fit our needs. Most importantly, we are excited to meet you, and see if you are a great fit for our team. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
Loft Orbital is revolutionizing access to space by building reliable, shareable satellites that drastically reduce the time and complexity traditionally required to get to orbit. We operate satellites, fly customer payloads, and handle entire missions from end-to-end. We’re a close-knit team of space enthusiasts, software experts, and cutting-edge technologists, all working together to make space simple for our customers.
 
As a Cloud Infrastructure Engineer on our Cloud Infrastructure Team, you’ll play a pivotal role in maintaining and scaling our ground segment infrastructure. You’ll collaborate across development, operations, and IT to ensure the integration, delivery, and reliability of services that support our space operations on Earth and in orbit.
 
This is an exciting opportunity to work on cutting-edge technology and help build modern automated space infrastructure. This is not your typical SRE role, we apply DevOps principles even to spacecraft control. Yes, we call it SatDevOps, and we’ll train you to operate our satellites!

lists.content:
• Collaborate with developers and satellite operators to foster a strong SatDevOps culture.
  • Design, implement, and maintain scalable, reliable, and secure infrastructure in a hybrid cloud environment.
  • Improve our developer experience by building better tools, workflows, and environments.
  • Lead efforts to automate and optimize systems, including CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure provisioning (IaC), and deployment workflows.
  • Own and evolve our observability stack (metrics, tracing, logs) to improve usability and performance. Grafana-centric ecosystems are a plus.
  • Implement and advocate for best practices in software reliability, fault tolerance, and performance tuning.
  • Proactively identify, investigate, and resolve system reliability issues, performing root cause analyses and implementing long-term fixes.
  • Partner with teams to design and operate Software Defined Network (SDN) solutions.
  • Contribute to a collaborative and inclusive team culture where respectful debate and continuous learning are celebrated.

• Strong experience with public cloud infrastructure, ideally GCP.
  • Deep expertise in Kubernetes, architecture, deployment, ops, and resource optimization.
  • Demonstrated ability to design and build scalable, highly available systems.
  • Familiarity with Software Defined Networking (SDN) concepts and tools.
  • Experience implementing and maintaining observability stacks (Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, etc.).
  • Proficiency in at least one backend language: Go, Python, Rust, C/C++, or Java.
  • Deep understanding and hands-on experience with DevOps practices: CI/CD, infrastructure as code (IaC), and automation.
  • Proven track record of working in fast-paced, high-growth technical environments.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to operate independently with a proactive, results-driven mindset.
  • Strong communication skills; thrives in a multicultural, cross-functional team.

• Hands-on experience with GitOps frameworks (ArgoCD, FluxCD).
  • Interest or experience in FinOps and cost-optimized architectures.
  • Understanding of orchestration in resource-constrained environments, like space systems.
  • Knowledge of systems engineering tools and SDLC governance.
  • Familiarity with security practices, vulnerability scanning, threat detection, risk mitigation.

• Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success
  • Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best
  • Health and life insurance, we care about your health
  • Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand)
  • Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences
  • Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together
  • Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
Customer Delivery Engineers (CDEs) own the end-to-end deployment and execution of customer satellite missions at Loft. We serve as the primary technical interface to our customers and translate mission objectives into operational reality, from early requirements and ConOps development through commissioning, on-orbit operations, and continuous improvement.
 
CDEs operate real spacecraft and work directly with customers to build mission applications on top of Loft’s API and operational infrastructure. You will translate mission objectives into executable workflows, configurations, and tooling that ensure reliable, scalable on-orbit execution. You will sit at the intersection of satellite operations, customer engineering, software development, systems engineering, and program execution, delivering meaningful outcomes for every mission you support.

Wanna join the adventure?
Loft Orbital is making space simple, giving commercial, defense, and government customers fast, reliable access to orbit through a standardized satellite platform. Our Hub and Cockpit products cut the complexity of traditional satellite missions, reducing time-to-orbit from years to months as we build a growing, heterogeneous fleet in LEO with increasing onboard AI and compute.
As Director, Embedded Systems & FPGA Engineering, you will shape the technical foundations that determine how Loft’s hardware, embedded software, onboard software, and operational systems work together. This is an opportunity to define the abstraction layers and engineering interfaces that let teams move faster without sacrificing robustness, reliability, or system understanding. You will help create a platform that can evolve across processors, FPGAs, operating systems, hypervisors, RISC-V, Rust, and future technologies without forcing unnecessary changes through every layer of the stack.

lists.content:
• Own the ESW and FPGA roadmap and technical direction across Loft’s satellite platforms.
  • Define HW-abstraction architecture and interfaces across FPGA, embedded software, onboard software, and operational layers.
  • Drive hardware-agnostic and reusable platform capabilities where they improve team independence and allow HW and technology to evolve.
  • Enable the ESW and FPGA leads through clear direction, decision context, coaching, and removal of organizational or technical blockers.
  • Set expectations for architecture, design reviews, code quality, testing, verification, documentation, and operational readiness.
  • Build the core engineering foundation for Linux, Yocto/OpenEmbedded, CI/CD, reproducible builds, and secure or sovereign environments.
  • Guide technology choices involving hypervisors, RISC-V, Rust, and other platform technologies when they create durable value.
  • Act as the face of ESW and FPGA and the triage point for company-wide technical issues, dependencies, and trade-offs.
  • Manage and develop geographically distributed leads and teams, including hiring, mentorship, performance management, and team health.
  • Represent the organization with customers, partners, and government or defense stakeholders when formal assurance and documentation are required.

• 10+ years of experience in embedded systems, FPGA, firmware, or closely related engineering, including delivery of mission-critical hardware or software.
  • Proven experience leading and managing technical teams, including geographically distributed teams.
  • Deep experience with FPGA design, embedded C/C++, real-time systems, and HW/SW integration.
  • Experience designing HW abstractions and hardware-agnostic interfaces from both technical and architectural perspectives.
  • Strong Linux kernel and embedded Linux experience, including low-level integration, drivers, boot, or system debugging.
  • Strong Yocto/OpenEmbedded and CI/CD experience, including build infrastructure, automated testing, and reproducible releases.
  • Experience building secure and sovereign environments, including trust boundaries, secure boot, signing, controlled dependencies, or related security architecture.
  • Experience with hypervisors, RISC-V, ARM and Rust development environments.
  • Track record of making sound trade-offs across reliability, performance, security, schedule, and technology evolution.
  • Collaborative, solution-minded leadership with the ability to enable leads, manage people with empathy and accountability, and act as a trusted cross-company technical representative.

• Experience with spacecraft avionics, command and data handling (C&DH), payload interfaces, or satellite flight systems.
  • Experience in New Space or satellite manufacturing, particularly standardized, modular, or repeatable satellite platforms.
  • Experience with radiation-tolerant or radiation-hardened design and an understanding of the space environment.
  • Experience with real-time operating systems such as RTEMS, FreeRTOS, or VxWorks.
  • Experience with high-speed interfaces such as Ethernet, SpaceWire, SpaceFibre, CAN, PCIe, USB, or MIL-STD-1553.
  • Experience with ARM-based embedded systems, U-Boot, ARM Trusted Firmware, device-tree overlays, or secure boot implementation.
  • Experience contributing to upstream Linux or maintaining kernel modules, platform drivers, or low-level middleware.
  • Experience with hypervisor isolation, virtualized I/O, partitioning, or mixed-criticality system design.
  • Experience using RISC-V or Rust in production, platform, tooling, or security-sensitive environments.
  • Exposure to onboard AI/ML compute or edge-processing hardware.
  • Experience supporting government or defense programs with formal assurance, security, sovereignty, and documentation requirements.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

Most importantly, we are excited to meet you, and see if you are a great fit for our team. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

descriptionPlain:
Role Overview
The Director of Design-to-Manufacturing (D2M) leads the organization responsible for transforming product and program requirements into controlled, validated, scalable manufacturing and test systems capable of supporting satellite production, integration, verification, and launch readiness. This person ensures engineering intent is developed for production while developing the team through technical guidance, operational excellence, and design-for-excellence feedback to engineering.
The Director provides organizational and technical leadership across three D2M sub-domains :
Manufacturing Systems & MGSE
Verification & Validation Test Engineering 
Test Platform & EGSEThe Director establishes the D2M technical operating model connecting Product Engineering to D2M to AIT Operations, ensuring engineering intent can be repeatedly built, integrated, tested, supported, and improved throughout the product lifecycle.
 
Own the industrialization of Orbitworks' products from engineering definition through manufacturing and test readiness, ensuring satellite designs can be repeatedly manufactured, integrated, verified, and sustained at the required quality, schedule, cost, and production rate.
description:
Role Overview

The Director of Design-to-Manufacturing (D2M) leads the organization responsible for transforming product and program requirements into controlled, validated, scalable manufacturing and test systems capable of supporting satellite production, integration, verification, and launch readiness. This person ensures engineering intent is developed for production while developing the team through technical guidance, operational excellence, and design-for-excellence feedback to engineering.

The Director provides organizational and technical leadership across three D2M sub-domains :

Manufacturing Systems & MGSE
Verification & Validation Test Engineering
Test Platform & EGSE

The Director establishes the D2M technical operating model connecting Product Engineering to D2M to AIT Operations, ensuring engineering intent can be repeatedly built, integrated, tested, supported, and improved throughout the product lifecycle.
 
Own the industrialization of Orbitworks' products from engineering definition through manufacturing and test readiness, ensuring satellite designs can be repeatedly manufactured, integrated, verified, and sustained at the required quality, schedule, cost, and production rate.

lists.content:
• Lead manufacturing and test teams: Manage Manufacturing Systems & Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE), Verification & Validation Test Engineering, and Test Platforms & Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE).
  • Turn engineering requirements into production-ready processes: Oversee work instructions, bills of materials, routings, assembly workflows, tooling, fixtures, and process validation.
  • Ensure test readiness: Oversee test methods, procedures, scripts, limits, configurations, coverage, and verification evidence.
  • Own test infrastructure readiness: Guide the development, validation, deployment, and maintenance of test benches, instrumentation, automation, networking, and spacecraft interfaces.
  • Review designs for manufacturability and testability: Work with mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering to identify constraints early and reduce rework.
  • Resolve manufacturing and test issues: Coordinate root-cause investigations, troubleshoot bottlenecks, and drive corrective actions.
  • Manage priorities and performance: Track readiness, quality, schedule, cost, throughput, risks, and resource needs.
  • Standardize and scale operations: Establish reusable tooling, test platforms, common standards, and predictable handoffs to Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT).
  • Coach and develop the team: Clarify ownership, strengthen technical leadership, and improve cross-functional collaboration.

• Strong manufacturing engineering and test engineering experience, translating complex designs into practical manufacturing and verification systems.
  • MGSE and EGSE expertise, including development, implementation, validation, and ongoing support.
  • Experience with hardware-in-the-loop/software-in-the-loop (HIL/SIL) or similarly complex integration and test environments.
  • Practical Design for Manufacturing, Assembly and Test (DFM/DFA/DFT) knowledge, with examples of influencing design decisions.
  • Proven technical team leadership and coaching, ideally across multiple engineering disciplines.
  • Strong collaboration across engineering, production, quality, supply chain, and programs.
  • Hands-on problem-solving and delivery under pressure, supported by examples of shipping complex hardware and resolving real production issues.

• Direct satellite or aerospace manufacturing experience.
  • Electronics or defence/DoD manufacturing experience involving complex, high-reliability systems.
  • Familiarity with ERP/MES systems for production workflows, reporting, and traceability.
  • Experience with agile or concurrent engineering, rapid prototyping, and iterative engineering-to-manufacturing handoffs.
  • Knowledge of AS9100 and ISO 9001 quality standards.

description:
Wanna join the adventure?

We are looking for a Director of Business Development, Americas to drive our next phase of commercial growth. This is a senior, highly autonomous business development and market creation role focused on identifying commercial space companies, emerging constellation operators, and strategic partners—and turning early relationships into funded missions and long-term programs.

You will create opportunities from the ground up. You’ll understand where companies are headed, identify where Loft can help, bring technical and commercial stakeholders together, and shape opportunities from early concepts into pathfinders, first missions, repeat spacecraft, or constellation-scale programs.

You will work closely with senior leadership and teams across sales engineering, product, engineering, mission operations, and our international organization. You'll be equally comfortable engaging founders and CEOs, CTOs and VPs of Engineering, and technical program leaders.

The best opportunities don't begin as traditional sales opportunities—they begin with a customer trying to solve a difficult problem.

lists.content:
• Market Development: Identify high-potential companies, emerging constellations, and new mission opportunities across the Americas. Build relationships early and develop a deep understanding of customer strategy, funding, technical roadmaps, and mission plans.

  • New Business Creation: Proactively originate opportunities rather than relying primarily on inbound leads or established accounts. Identify where Loft's infrastructure can solve a customer problem before a formal requirement or RFP exists.

  • Strategic Selling: Build relationships with founders, CEOs, CTOs, engineering leaders, mission owners, and other senior decision-makers. Understand their objectives and shape solutions that align Loft's capabilities with their broader business and technical strategy.

  • Program Development: Lead opportunities from an initial concept through pathfinder missions, demonstrations, first missions, and ultimately repeat or constellation-scale programs.

  • Full-Cycle Business Development: Own opportunities through qualification, solution development, proposal, commercial negotiation, contracting, and close, partnering with the appropriate internal teams throughout the process.

  • Strategic Partnerships: Develop relationships with spacecraft manufacturers, launch providers, data and analytics companies, systems integrators, and other ecosystem partners that can create new customer opportunities or expand Loft's reach.

  • Account Expansion: Turn successful initial missions into long-term customer relationships. Identify opportunities for additional spacecraft, missions, payloads, services, or constellation deployments.

  • Market Intelligence: Maintain a strong understanding of the commercial space ecosystem, including emerging companies, funding activity, new mission architectures, competitive dynamics, and evolving customer needs.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Bring together technical, commercial, and operational stakeholders to turn ambiguous customer needs into executable programs.

• 8+ years of experience in business development, strategic sales, partnerships, or an equivalent customer-facing role, with a strong track record of originating and closing complex opportunities.

  • Deep understanding of the space industry and commercial space ecosystem, including satellite operators, spacecraft manufacturers, launch providers, space data companies, and related technology and infrastructure providers.

  • Demonstrated success as a net-new business developer and hunter—someone who has created opportunities and opened new customers rather than primarily managing an established book of business.

  • Experience selling complex technical products, services, or infrastructure through a consultative or solutions-oriented approach.

  • Ability to build credibility with senior executive and technical stakeholders, from founders and CEOs to CTOs, engineering leaders, and program owners.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguous, early-stage opportunities where the customer need, solution, or buying process may not yet be fully defined.

  • Experience owning complex opportunities through the full business development and sales cycle, including solution development, proposals, commercial negotiations, and contracting.

  • Strong commercial judgment and the ability to prioritize opportunities based on strategic value, probability of success, and long-term potential.

  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and negotiation skills.

  • Willingness to travel regularly to meet customers and partners across the Americas.

• Existing relationships with commercial constellation companies, emerging space companies, or strategic players in the Americas space ecosystem.

  • Experience selling satellite, spacecraft, mission, launch, data, connectivity, or other space infrastructure services.

  • Experience developing strategic partnerships or channel relationships that generate measurable commercial opportunities.

  • Technical background in aerospace, space systems, engineering, or a related field.

  • Experience working with venture-backed or rapidly scaling companies.

  • Experience across multiple segments of the space ecosystem rather than a single product or customer category.

  • Experience with mission-as-a-service, satellite-as-a-service, hosted payloads, or other infrastructure-based space business models.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks

  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver

You’ll understand where companies are headed, identify where Loft can help, bring technical and commercial stakeholders together, and shape opportunities from early concepts into pathfinders, first missions, repeat spacecraft, or constellation-scale programs.

You will work closely with senior leadership and teams across sales engineering, product, engineering, mission operations, and our international organization. You'll be equally comfortable engaging founders and CEOs, CTOs and VPs of Engineering, and technical program leaders.

The best opportunities don't begin as traditional sales opportunities—they begin with a customer trying to solve a difficult problem.

Loft Orbital is making space simple. We build and operate reliable, shareable satellites that give customers a faster, simpler path to orbit. By combining flight-proven spacecraft platforms with our own hardware and software, we make it easier to deploy missions in space.

lists.content:
• Design, develop, and maintain hardware abstraction layers (HALs), device drivers, and board support packages (BSPs).
  • Develop and optimize hardware interfaces, peripherals, and data transfer mechanisms.
  • Lead hands-on board bring-up, hardware/software integration, and low-level debugging.
  • Write reliable, maintainable C/C++ software for embedded Linux and/or RTOS platforms.
  • Diagnose complex issues using hardware documentation, debugging tools, and direct hardware testing.
  • Develop unit and integration tests to validate software on target hardware.
  • Collaborate with hardware, FPGA, and systems engineers to deliver robust, flight-ready solutions.

• 5+ years of professional embedded software development experience in C and/or C++.
  • Strong hands-on experience designing and developing HALs and low-level device drivers.
  • Experience with BSPs, register-level programming, and hardware/peripheral configuration.
  • Proven experience with board bring-up, hardware/software integration, and low-level debugging.
  • Experience with embedded Linux and/or RTOS platforms.
  • Understanding of hardware interfaces and protocols such as UART, SPI, I²C, DMA, Ethernet, LVDS, or SpaceWire.
  • Experience with debugging tools such as GDB, JTAG, logic analyzers, or oscilloscopes.
  • Ability to read schematics and datasheets and troubleshoot issues across hardware and software.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, ownership, and ability to work across multidisciplinary teams.

• Linux kernel internals, kernel-space driver development, and device trees.
  • Embedded Linux build systems such as Yocto or Buildroot.
  • ARM-based SoCs and FPGA integration.
  • Aerospace, spaceflight, or safety-critical software experience.
  • Radiation mitigation techniques, including Single Event Upset (SEU) handling.
  • Embedded virtualization or hypervisor experience.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents

  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations

descriptionPlain:
Role Overview

Orbitworks is looking for a hands-on Environmental Test Technician to support the testing and qualification of satellite hardware and spacecraft systems.
In this role, you’ll work closely with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and test teams to prepare hardware, configure test equipment, execute environmental test campaigns, and ensure test activities are completed safely, accurately, and in accordance with approved procedures.
You’ll support a range of environmental tests designed to verify that spacecraft hardware can withstand the conditions experienced during launch and operation in space. This is a practical, detail-oriented role suited to someone who enjoys working directly with hardware, test equipment, and engineering teams in a fast-paced technical environment.
description:
Role Overview

Orbitworks is looking for a hands-on Environmental Test Technician to support the testing and qualification of satellite hardware and spacecraft systems.

In this role, you’ll work closely with engineering, manufacturing, quality, and test teams to prepare hardware, configure test equipment, execute environmental test campaigns, and ensure test activities are completed safely, accurately, and in accordance with approved procedures.

You’ll support a range of environmental tests designed to verify that spacecraft hardware can withstand the conditions experienced during launch and operation in space. This is a practical, detail-oriented role suited to someone who enjoys working directly with hardware, test equipment, and engineering teams in a fast-paced technical environment.

lists.content:
• Set up and prepare spacecraft hardware, components, and test articles for environmental testing.
  • Support the execution of environmental test campaigns including vibration, thermal, thermal vacuum, and other qualification or acceptance testing.
  • Install and configure test fixtures, sensors, accelerometers, thermocouples, cables, and data acquisition equipment.
  • Prepare test chambers, vibration systems, and supporting equipment in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Perform pre-test inspections and verify that test configurations match engineering documentation.
  • Execute test procedures while monitoring hardware and test equipment throughout the test.
  • Record test parameters, observations, anomalies, and results accurately.
  • Support engineers in troubleshooting hardware, instrumentation, or test-equipment issues.
  • Assist with post-test inspections and hardware removal following completion of testing.
  • Maintain test equipment, tooling, fixtures, cables, and laboratory areas.
  • Support equipment calibration and ensure test assets remain within their required calibration periods.
  • Follow safety procedures and maintain a clean, organized, and controlled test environment.

Test Preparation:
Prepare hardware, instrumentation, fixtures, and test facilities for environmental testing.

Test Execution:
Execute approved environmental test procedures safely and accurately while monitoring test conditions and hardware performance.

Instrumentation:
Install and verify sensors, measurement equipment, data acquisition systems, and associated cabling.

Documentation:
Maintain accurate test records, configuration information, observations, and test results.

Equipment Maintenance:
Support the maintenance, calibration, and readiness of environmental test equipment and laboratory tooling.

Troubleshooting:
Work with engineers to identify and resolve issues encountered during test setup and execution.

Safety & Quality:
Ensure all activities are performed in accordance with safety, quality, configuration-control, and engineering requirements.

• Diploma, technical qualification, or Associate's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace, or a related technical field.
  • Hands-on experience working with mechanical, electrical, or test equipment in a technical environment.
  • Ability to follow detailed engineering procedures, work instructions, and test documentation.
  • Ability to read technical drawings, schematics, assembly drawings, and equipment instructions.
  • Experience using basic measurement and test equipment.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and practical problem-solving skills.
  • High attention to detail, particularly when working with sensitive or high-value hardware.

• Previous experience in environmental testing, aerospace testing, spacecraft testing, or another high-reliability industry.
  • Hands-on experience with vibration or shaker testing.
  • Experience with thermal or thermal vacuum chambers.
  • Experience installing accelerometers, thermocouples, strain gauges, or other test instrumentation.
  • Familiarity with data acquisition systems and test monitoring software.
  • Understanding of vibration, thermal, shock, or vacuum testing principles.
  • Experience working in cleanroom or controlled manufacturing environments.
  • Familiarity with spacecraft, satellite, aviation, defence, or advanced engineering hardware.
  • Experience working with calibrated equipment and controlled test documentation.
  • Basic knowledge of electrical troubleshooting and measurement equipment.

Wanna join the adventure?
Loft Orbital is looking for a Flight Dynamics Software Engineer to join the Ground Platform organization.
You'll work on a small and driven team, developing our flight dynamics software stack so that it can:
Scale to fly 50+ satellites in orbit in a highly automated, reliable, and safe (from a collision avoidance perspective) manner
Enable new conops and customer missions with demanding orbit determination, stationkeeping, and attitude performance requirements
We're looking for someone with a solid theoretical understanding of astrodynamics, operational flight-dynamics experience, and software-engineering foundations. If you enjoy solving hard problems and working in a fast-paced and supportive environment, we'd love to hear from you.
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for a Flight Dynamics Software Engineer to join the Ground Platform organization.

You'll work on a small and driven team, developing our flight dynamics software stack so that it can:

  • Scale to fly 50+ satellites in orbit in a highly automated, reliable, and safe (from a collision avoidance perspective) manner
  • Enable new conops and customer missions with demanding orbit determination, stationkeeping, and attitude performance requirements

We're looking for someone with a solid theoretical understanding of astrodynamics, operational flight-dynamics experience, and software-engineering foundations. If you enjoy solving hard problems and working in a fast-paced and supportive environment, we'd love to hear from you.

We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

lists.content:
• Implement and improve upon algorithms for orbit determination, orbit propagation, maneuver planning (stationkeeping/orbit transfer), conjunction assessment, collision avoidance, and attitude modeling, contributing to our open-source astrodynamics tooling that powers both flight operations and simulation work across the company
  • Develop and maintain the in-house flight dynamics ground software backend applications that compute, store, and serve our fleet’s ephemerides, maneuvers, conjunctions, target orbits, etc
  • Interface with systems and mission engineers to help translate technical mission requirements and customer demands into operational outcomes in orbit
  • Support satellite operations engineers by providing astrodynamics expertise during LEOP/anomalies/conjunction response and assisting with configuring our software stack for various customer missions

• Bachelor's degree in physics or an engineering discipline
  • Deep technical understanding of some of the following topics: orbital mechanics, state estimation, spacecraft maneuver planning, conjunction assessment, and spacecraft attitude modeling
  • Fundamentals of numerical methods: solvers, optimization, and simulation techniques
  • Experience with designing and developing software libraries and backend services, in Python
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

• Master’s degree in physics or an engineering discipline
  • Proficiency in astrodynamics tools such as STK, Astrogator, GMAT, OreKit, Monte, Copernicus, OpenSpaceToolkit, or equivalent
  • Demonstrated practical experience in spacecraft constellation flight dynamics operations
  • Demonstrated practical experience building high-performance backend software applications and/or libraries
  • Capable of solving complex problems within a highly collaborative environment

• Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success
  • Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best
  • Health and life insurance, we care about your health
  • Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand)
  • Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences
  • Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together
  • Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

lists.content:
• Implement and improve upon algorithms for orbit determination, orbit propagation, maneuver planning (stationkeeping/orbit transfer), conjunction assessment, collision avoidance, and attitude modeling, contributing to our open-source astrodynamics tooling that powers both flight operations and simulation work across the company
  • Develop and maintain the in-house flight dynamics ground software backend applications that compute, store, and serve our fleet’s ephemerides, maneuvers, conjunctions, target orbits, etc
  • Interface with systems and mission engineers to help translate technical mission requirements and customer demands into operational outcomes in orbit
  • Support satellite operations engineers by providing astrodynamics expertise during LEOP/anomalies/conjunction response and assisting with configuring our software stack for various customer missions

• Bachelor's degree in physics or an engineering discipline
  • Deep technical understanding of some of the following topics: orbital mechanics, state estimation, spacecraft maneuver planning, conjunction assessment, and spacecraft attitude modeling

• Master’s degree in physics or an engineering discipline

lists.content:
• Build the Marketplace storefront, partner portal, and admin tooling.
  • Design and implement the APIs and services behind them: catalog, onboarding, entitlements, and metering.
  • Integrate with our mission platform for authentication, workflow triggers, and solution deployment in close collaboration with engineering teams.
  • Build connectors for third-party constellations and data providers.
  • Own quality: tests, CI/CD, monitoring.

• 4+ years building and shipping full-stack products.
  • Experience with Sprint development.
  • Strong TypeScript/React or Vue on the front end and solid backend experience in either Python, Go, or Node.
  • Cloud-native by default (we run on GCP): containers/kubernetes, managed services, infrastructure as code.
  • Comfortable with API design, OAuth, and multi-tenant authorization.
  • Fluent with AI-assisted development workflows and expected to use them.
  • You have shipped a zero-to-one product, ideally a marketplace, developer platform, or SaaS portal, and you like small teams with large scope.

• Billing integrations (Stripe or similar).
  • Geospatial or earth observation exposure.
  • Security-minded engineering (tenant isolation, audit trails).
  • Experience in the architecture of modern systems.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver

lists.content:

  • Take responsibility for the reliability and performance of Loft's ground platform infrastructure, including message queues, CI/CD, and observability
  • Have the opportunity to take part in spacecraft operations through SatDevOps rotations, occasionally helping investigate anomalies and supporting real‑time incident response when needed

  • Experience with message queues and streaming technologies (NATS)
  • Knowledge of DevOps and observability tools (Helm, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Loki, etc)

  • Frontend development with Vue and Web Components

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA

  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

salaryDescription: State law requires us to tell you the base compensation range for this role, which is $140,000- $190,000 per year. This is determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.  The salary range for this role is intentionally wide as we evaluate individuals based on their unique experience and abilities to fit our needs. Most importantly, we are excited to meet you, and see if you are a great fit for our team. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

description:
About the Role

Orbitworks is seeking a Senior Industrial Engineer to lead the industrialization of our satellite products and build the production capability needed to deliver them at scale. Based at our KEZAD facility in Abu Dhabi and reporting to the SVP of Operations, you'll connect product design, assembly and test methods, infrastructure, equipment, workforce capability, and material availability into a working industrial solution for a medium-mix, medium-to-low-volume production environment.

You'll own the industrialization workstream end-to-end — from product assessment and partner transfer through new product introduction (NPI), deployment, production readiness, ramp-up, and handover — while personally developing capacity models and industrial solutions and working hands-on on the production floor. This is a strategic, hands-on individual-contributor role: you'll need strong technical judgment, the ability to influence without formal authority, and the persistence to see implementation through. As the business grows, scope can expand into broader portfolio ownership, technical leadership, and building out an industrialization team.

lists.content:
• Own the industrialization strategy and integrated delivery plan — translating product, demand, and business objectives into rate targets, work packages, owners, milestones, resources, budget needs, dependencies, risks, and acceptance criteria.
  • Work with Engineering/D2M and AIT to define build sequence, work breakdown, routings, assembly and test flows, and manufacturing data needs, driving design for manufacture, assembly, test, access, and repeatability.
  • Build version-controlled capacity models from execution data, time studies, engineering estimates, and partner data, and balance cells and workflows to the required production rate.
  • Develop layouts, workstations, material flow, buffers, WIP policies, cleanroom zoning, and kitting interfaces, comparing fixed-station, cellular, parallel, and flow approaches against product and rate constraints.
  • Define and deliver industrial asset work packages for ground support equipment, test assets, utilities, and facility changes, driving procurement, installation, commissioning, and handover.
  • Lead the industrialization interface with external partners — agreeing technical deliverables, owners, dates, and acceptance criteria for product data, methods, tooling, training, and test interfaces.
  • Lead industrial readiness assessments, closing process, equipment, documentation, training, supply, and infrastructure gaps, and securing production-release decisions through Orbitworks' readiness and change reviews.
  • Lead pilots and support ramp-up on the production floor, validating assumptions, resolving constraints, and demonstrating agreed rate, mix, quality, and resource performance.
  • Define rate, lead-time, WIP, capacity, labor, quality, and constraint metrics, and drive improvements that produce sustained, system-level results.
  • Develop investment and resource options, lead delivery reviews, coach contributors, and establish reusable models, standards, and decision records.

• 7–12 years in industrial, manufacturing, or production engineering, with an engineering degree or equivalent demonstrated capability.
  • Direct, hands-on experience in satellite assembly, integration, test, or comparable space hardware production, with industrialization responsibility at the system or subsystem level. General aerospace experience alone doesn't meet this requirement.
  • A track record of owning an integrated industrialization workstream through deployment, ramp-up, and acceptance, with plans, milestones, resource or investment decisions, recovery actions, and measured outcomes to show for it.
  • Strong capacity modeling and line balancing skills — building auditable models of mixed-product demand, process precedence, labor skills, equipment occupancy, calendars, variability, rework, and bottlenecks.
  • Production engineering depth: routings, work instructions, tooling, process control, work measurement, layout, material flow, WIP, and producibility, with the ability to translate drawings and test requirements into industrial requirements.
  • Experience defining and delivering production or test capability through requirements, procurement, commissioning, acceptance, and operational handover.
  • Skill in extracting usable technical inputs from external partners, tracking assumptions and gaps, and following through until the local production solution works.
  • Proven ability to manage cross-functional work packages, dependencies, risks, and commitments as an individual contributor, without relying on formal line authority. Formal people-management experience is not required.
  • Strong spreadsheet and data analysis skills, with models that have traceable sources, units, assumptions, and actual-versus-plan checks.
  • Understanding of traceability, controlled baselines, manufacturing/test readiness, and change impact in high-reliability hardware.
  • Clear technical English, concise written communication, effective shop-floor engagement, willingness to work onsite in Abu Dhabi, and the ability to travel to partners as needed.

• Experience ramping a LEO constellation from first units into repeat production.
  • Having commissioned a cleanroom, production area, or major test capability, including utilities, safety, and contamination control.
  • Experience phasing new products or upgrades into a shared industrial asset while protecting existing delivery commitments.
  • Discrete-event simulation and optimization experience for problems beyond spreadsheet capability.
  • Practical experience with MES, ERP, PLM, manufacturing BOM, routing, and dashboard tools.
  • Ability to build labor, recurring cost, capex, and make-versus-buy scenarios with Finance and Supply Chain.
  • Applied Lean or Six Sigma experience in complex production environments, with measured results (certification alone isn't a differentiator).
  • Experience assessing supplier process capacity and supporting local supplier capability development.
  • A track record of coaching and raising colleagues' capability without relying on formal management authority.

description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital builds and operates satellites, and behind every mission is a web of business systems: ERP, PLM, MES, issue tracking, finance, and a growing toolkit of in-house software. Each holds part of the story; none of them tells the whole thing. We’re looking for an Information Systems Data Engineer to connect them. You’ll design Loft’s centralized database, build the pipelines that feed it, and deliver the reporting that shows how we’re really performing. If you like writing code that turns messy, scattered data into something people actually rely on, we’d love to talk.

lists.content:
• Design, build, and maintain a centralized SQL Server database and the data model that connects Loft’s business systems
  • Develop and operate Python/SQL ETL pipelines from NetSuite, Arena, ION, Jira, and other sources, managed in GitLab with CI/CD
  • Build Power BI dashboards and reports that monitor operational performance and KPIs
  • Develop and support NetSuite customizations, including SuiteScripts, workflows, and saved searches
  • Partner with Operations, Finance, Engineering, and IT to gather requirements and deliver integrations and tools
  • Document systems and data flows, and promote data quality, governance, and change control

• 3+ years of experience in data engineering, business systems, or a related technical role
  • Proficiency in Python for scripting, automation, and data processing
  • Hands-on experience with GitLab and CI/CD processes
  • Experience building and maintaining ETL pipelines
  • Strong SQL skills and experience with relational database design and management
  • Clear communicator who can translate business needs into technical solutions
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software or Computer Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent professional experience

• NetSuite SuiteScript and workflow development
  • NetSuite saved searches, SuiteQL, or SuiteAnalytics
  • Microsoft SQL Server
  • Power BI (data modeling, DAX)
  • Experience with PLM, MES, or Jira data
  • Experience applying AI/LLM tools to data or systems work

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance

description:
About the role

Orbitworks is looking for an IT Administrator to own the systems, networks and technology that support our satellite manufacturing operations.

You will keep our infrastructure reliable, secure and recoverable while providing hands-on IT support across our offices, labs and cleanroom. Your scope will include backup and disaster recovery, connectivity, endpoint management and the technical delivery of business continuity.

This is an individual contributor role with ownership of the IT function and support from external technology and security partners. It suits someone who enjoys working independently, solving practical problems and balancing daily support with longer-term infrastructure improvements.

lists.content:
• Own IT infrastructure and connectivity: Maintain and troubleshoot networks, firewalls, VPNs and virtualized environments. Manage resilient connectivity across our sites, including multiple internet connections and WAN failover.

  • Manage backup and disaster recovery: Own backups across virtual machines, Google Workspace, Dropbox and onsite storage. Verify daily completion, resolve failures and maintain offsite and immutable backup copies.

  • Test recovery and continuity: Run monthly restore drills, isolated cyber recovery testing and quarterly continuity exercises. Document results, address gaps and keep recovery procedures current.

  • Maintain emergency site readiness: Ensure the alternative operating site has the connectivity, backup access and infrastructure needed to support business continuity. Coordinate IT power resilience with Facilities.

  • Strengthen security: Work with external security partners to address assessment findings, harden infrastructure and improve access controls, MFA and endpoint security.

  • Deliver daily IT support: Resolve hardware, software, permissions and collaboration tool issues. Configure and manage Mac and Windows laptops, mobile devices and MDM.

  • Support employees and technical teams: Coordinate onboarding and offboarding with the People team, maintain meeting room AV systems and support devices used in labs, manufacturing and the cleanroom.

  • Manage vendors, documentation and reporting: Coordinate external support, maintain runbooks and offline emergency instructions, support audits and provide clear infrastructure and continuity updates to leadership.

  • Support growth: Deliver infrastructure improvements and help set up new office and lab environments as Orbitworks scales.

• At least 6 years of IT experience, including 2 years owning infrastructure as the primary or sole administrator.

  • Hands-on experience with backup, disaster recovery and restore testing.

  • Strong corporate networking skills, including LAN/WAN, VPNs, firewalls and multi-WAN failover.

  • Practical experience administering Google Workspace.

  • Experience with single sign-on, mobile device management and access controls across Mac and Windows environments.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to prioritize and resolve issues independently.

  • Clear written communication, with the ability to produce useful technical documentation and explain risks, progress and recovery readiness to business leaders.

• Experience with Cisco Meraki and Synology, including high-availability storage and Active Backup.

  • Exposure to business continuity programmes or ISO 22301.

  • Experience supporting manufacturing, laboratory or cleanroom environments.

  • Linux desktop and virtualization experience.

  • Familiarity with Jira and Confluence.

    •

You’ll own a critical function in a growing satellite manufacturing business, working closely with engineering, industrial operations and business teams. Your work will directly support reliable operations and strengthen our ability to recover from disruption.

As Orbitworks grows, there is an opportunity to develop toward broader IT and security leadership and help build the future IT team.

additionalPlain:
Who We Are

Loft Orbital builds “shareable” satellites, providing a fast & simple path to orbit for organizations that require access to space. Powered by our hardware & software products, we operate satellites, fly customer payloads onboard, and handle entire missions from end to end - significantly reducing the lead-time and risk of a traditional space mission.

Our standard interface enables us to fly multiple customer payloads on the same satellite, with capabilities such as earth imagery, weather & climate /science data collection, IoT connectivity, in-orbit demonstrations, and national security missions. Our customers trust us to manage their space infrastructure, so they can focus on what matters most to them: operating their mission and collecting their data.

At Loft, you’ll be given the autonomy and ownership to solve significant challenges, but with a close-knit and supportive team at your back. We believe that diversity and community are the foundation of an open culture. We are committed to hiring the best people regardless of background and make their time at Loft the most fulfilling period of their career.

We value kind, supportive and team-oriented collaborators. It is also crucial for us that you are a problem solver and a great communicator. As our team is international, you will need strong English skills to better collaborate, easily communicate complex ideas and convey important messages.

With 3 satellites on-orbit and a wave of exciting missions launching soon, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France.

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.


 *Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Loft, we value respectful debate and people who aren’t afraid to challenge assumptions.  We strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check all the boxes.

Who We Are

Loft: Space Made Simple. 

Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
Loft Orbital's mission is to make space simple. We deploy customer missions on our satellite infrastructure so our customers can focus on their applications instead of the spacecraft underneath them. The Customer Delivery team turns signed contracts into working missions on orbit and supports our customers from start to finish.
As a Mission Manager on the Customer Delivery team, you lead the delivery of customer missions from contract signature to deployment on orbit. You own the Mission Development Plan and schedule, drive the work across engineering, product, and operations teams, and keep the customer and Loft aligned on where things stand. You will work alongside our Customer Delivery Engineers (CDEs), who design and execute each customer mission, by building the development plans and capability portfolio they draw on to deliver value to our customers. You will also manage the Customer Offering Portfolio that defines what Loft can deliver and drive quality, visibility, and consistency in how new capabilities are deployed to our customer offering. This role is well suited to someone who has delivered complex technical programs to external customers and wants to own missions flying in orbit.

lists.content:
• Own the Mission Development Plan for assigned missions: identify all work required to deploy and execute the mission, break it down into committed work packages with contributing teams, and drive it to completion against launch-anchored deadlines and the customer milestones
  • Manage the customer relationship for mission delivery: engage with customers day to day, up to the executive level, on mission scope, schedule, and capability tradeoffs
  • Manage the Customer Offering Portfolio: maintain the catalog of capabilities Loft can draw on to execute customer missions, identify deltas between the portfolio and upcoming mission needs, and drive new capability development with product and engineering teams
  • Partner with Customer Delivery Engineers to deliver customer value: CDEs execute the mission with the customer, and you ensure the capabilities, plans, and tooling they need are in place when they need them
  • Connect Customer Delivery to Loft's product organization by representing operational and customer constraints in product planning, and by managing the deployment of new features and capabilities into operational use
  • Drive cross-functional coordination and status clarity: run internal reviews with CDEs, report on development progress, risks, and blockers, and keep leadership and customers aligned on where things stand
  • Build the tools, templates, and workflows the Customer Delivery team needs to execute efficiently - often from a blank page, with Jira and spreadsheets - and right-size them for a small, fast-moving team

• 8+ years of professional experience in technical program, product, or engineering roles
  • 3+ years managing technical programs or missions delivered to external customers, from definition through delivery and operations
  • Experience deploying products into production or operational environments, including release readiness, cross-team dependency management, and post-deployment quality
  • Experience in the satellite or aerospace industry, with working knowledge of spacecraft systems, mission operations, or payload development
  • Experience owning the relationship with external customers day to day, including scope, schedule, and tradeoff conversations with executive-level stakeholders
  • Exceptional and proven technical aptitude: able to go deep with engineers on architecture and tradeoffs, and translate that fluently for customers and executives
  • Excellent and concise communication skills at all levels, from engineering deep dives to executive summaries, with the organization and prioritization skills to run multiple parallel workstreams in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable working with incomplete information and light process: you act with autonomy, help us make the right decisions at the right level, know when to escalate, and keep people informed
  • Fluent written and spoken English; our customers and half the Customer Delivery team are in the US

• Direct experience with satellite on-orbit operations, commissioning, or ground segment software
  • Technical leadership experience (leading engineers or technical teams, formally or informally)
  • Experience building or managing a product/capability portfolio, roadmap, or plan of record
  • Experience with international customers and distributed teams

• Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success
  • Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best
  • Health and life insurance, we care about your health
  • Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand)
  • Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences
  • Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together
  • Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft's AI for Space group is building the stack that runs real machine learning in orbit; turning raw sensor data into decisions on the satellite itself, so insight reaches the customer in minutes instead of hours.
The AI Engineering team is where models meet the spacecraft. We own the full path from a partner's trained model to something that actually runs — fast — on flight hardware: compiling ONNX models into optimized engines for each accelerator, the Space Inference Engine and its execution providers, the SDK that packages models for flight, and the perf tooling that proves a model fits its power, thermal, and latency budget before it ever leaves the ground. As we open the platform to a growing roster of defense and Earth-observation partners, the team's scope and the range of silicon we target are expanding fast.

As our ML Runtime Engineer, you'll own model compilation and the performance tooling behind it. We're looking for someone scrappy — the kind of engineer who takes an unfamiliar model and an unforgiving power budget, digs into the graph, and gets it running on real hardware without waiting for the path to be handed to them. You'll move between model compilation, runtime internals, quantization, and hardware-in-the-loop CI, sometimes in the same afternoon.

  • Remote sensing / large-image handling

  • Model-weight protection / secure execution

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
Loft’s Onboard Software group provides the on-orbit software that powers our satellite fleet — from the Linux services running on the hub processor, to the containerized workloads executing customer applications in low Earth orbit.
The Deployment & Runtime Environments team is where software meets the satellite. We own how software gets packaged, deployed, and executed onboard: from the tool that assembles and maintains mission-specific software stacks, to the Runtime Container Environment that lets partner and customer workloads run securely in orbit, to the Linux infrastructure that makes it all reliable. As more satellite programs come online and as we open our container runtime to a growing number of external workloads, the team’s scope is expanding fast.
We’re looking for someone scrappy — the kind of engineer who digs into an unfamiliar system, maps it out, and gets it shipped without needing the path handed to them. You’ll move between Linux internals, container runtimes, and CI pipelines, sometimes in the same afternoon.
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

  • Develop and harden our onboard Linux infrastructure: how services are deployed on the rootfs, what system manages their execution, and how we ensure reliable and recoverable Linux operation in orbit
  • Evolve our Runtime Container Environment — the container manager and the full stack around it (base images, container registry service) — enabling partner and customer workloads to run securely onboard our vehicles

  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines (GitLab-CI, Jenkins, or similar)
  • Proficiency with Git and collaborative development workflows
  • Experience with embedded or resource-constrained systems
  • Working Python

• Understanding of software deployment strategies for critical or hard-to-reach systems — OTA updates for cars, drones, or consumer hardware, or software updates on satellites — including concepts like golden images, A/B partitions, staged rollouts, and safe rollback
  • C++ knowledge
  • Experience with CUE (cuelang)
  • Familiarity with additional programming languages such as Go or Rust
  • Experience with embedded Linux: Yocto, device trees, systemd, and Linux on ARM platforms
  • Proficiency with unit test frameworks (e.g., pytest, Googletest, Unity)

  • Review code, provide clear feedback, and enforce adherence to established development processes, style guides, and design standards to maintain consistency and quality across the codebase.
  • Design and implement unit tests for both self-authored and peer-authored code.
  • Utilize version control systems to create feature branches, push code, and merge approved code into production branches.
  • Contribute to the onboard software architecture through design proposals and collaborative review
  • Participate in the review and enhancement of software development processes and design standards.
  • Coordinate with downstream teams on the release, distribution and adoption of latest releases.
  • In addition to responsibilities within onboard software, you’ll have the opportunity to directly be involved in operating our on-orbit fleet of satellites.

• 5+ years' software engineering experience, using programming languages including C/C++ (C++11 or newer) and Python.
  • Experience with version control systems such as Git
  • Experience with continuous integration tools (e.g., GitLab-CI, Jenkins).
  • Experience with build systems (e.g., Make, CMake).
  • Experience with library management and ABI/API version control.
  • Understanding of distributed architecture.
  • Familiarity with networking protocols (e.g., UDP, TCP, IP) and POSIX standards.
  • Experience in developing multi-threaded applications.

• Familiarity with additional programming languages, such as Go or Rust.
  • Experience with embedded Linux operation, including Yocto, device trees, systemd, and Linux on ARM platforms.
  • Proficiency with unit test frameworks (e.g., pytest, Googletest, Unity)
  • Experience with middleware framework (gRPC, ZMQ/NATS, etc.)
  • Experience with containerization technologies (Docker, K3S, systemd-nspawn)

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

descriptionBody:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft’s Onboard Software group provides the on-orbit software that powers our core products. This is responsible for monitoring and control of major space program elements, including:

  • Flight Products computational environments (including physical and virtual processors);

  • Interfaces with external equipment (imagers, RF, ISL); and

  • Interfaces with the spacecraft bus.

Hyperdrive is the common platform powering every onboard service across our spacecraft.
The team builds the core capabilities other onboard services need to run mission logic—from interactions and housekeeping to events, automated fault detection and recovery, and lifecycle management.
By making complex spacecraft software consistent, observable, and resilient, Hyperdrive helps teams move faster while keeping missions safe in orbit.

We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

Who We Are

Loft: Space Made Simple. 

Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
Loft's AI for Space group is building the stack that runs real machine learning in orbit; turning raw sensor data into decisions on the satellite itself, so insight reaches the customer in minutes instead of hours.
The AI Engineering team is where models meet the spacecraft. We own the full path from a partner's trained model to something that actually runs — fast — on flight hardware: compiling ONNX models into optimized engines for each accelerator, the Space Inference Engine and its execution providers, the SDK that packages models for flight, and the perf tooling that proves a model fits its power, thermal, and latency budget before it ever leaves the ground. As we open the platform to a growing roster of defense and Earth-observation partners, the team's scope and the range of silicon we target are expanding fast.

As our ML Runtime Engineer, you'll own model compilation and the performance tooling behind it. We're looking for someone scrappy — the kind of engineer who takes an unfamiliar model and an unforgiving power budget, digs into the graph, and gets it running on real hardware without waiting for the path to be handed to them. You'll move between model compilation, runtime internals, quantization, and hardware-in-the-loop CI, sometimes in the same afternoon.
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft’s Onboard Software group provides the on-orbit software that powers our satellite fleet — from the Linux services running on the Hub’s onboard computers, to the containerized workloads executing customer applications in low Earth orbit.

The Peripheral Services team owns the software that integrates third-party devices and payloads into Loft’s standardized satellite platform. We enable the control and monitoring of many key spacecraft components, including optical payloads, radios, power controllers, and GNSS receivers. Many of these components are reused across all satellite programs and form the building blocks of our onboard architecture.

The applications developed by our team handle the low-level communication protocol details, exposing the connected devices behind standardized APIs used across mission operations. The team is also responsible for the automation and orchestration that allows Loft to safely and reliably operate the equipment at scale.

In this role, you’ll help develop the software that connects diverse spacecraft hardware to the rest of the platform, and ultimately enables successful missions in orbit.

description:
Wanna Join the Adventure?
 
The Onboard Software Solutions Team is responsible for creating, configuring, and deploying all onboard software components dedicated to a program or mission.
