descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
At Loft, we are convinced that space programs should not have to be rebuilt from scratch every time. Our philosophy has been to productize them: we develop our own proprietary technology blocks, hardware and software, so that a customer payload can be integrated faster and more reliably than any bespoke program allows. That approach has delivered — it is why our customers reach orbit in months rather than years, and it is what makes working here different from working in the rest of the industry.
We are now taking the next step: launching and operating our own constellations, and building a new set of services on top of them. That includes a full product suite enabling third-party AI applications to run directly onboard our satellites, and a growing ecosystem of partners whose needs we have to understand and design for. Loft is expanding at a very high pace, and the range of what we build is expanding just as fast.
This is why Product Management matters so much here. Someone has to hold the whole picture — what is technically possible, what customers actually need, what we should build first — and turn it into something engineering and leadership can act on. As a Product Manager, you will own a significant perimeter and the autonomy that goes with it. We are growing the team precisely so that each of us can go deeper on our topics, anticipate rather than react, and have more impact across the company.
You will need to be comfortable talking to anyone here. In the same week you might sit with a system engineer to understand a design constraint, join a BD call with an institutional customer, and present a recommendation to the executive team. Ideas at Loft get discussed openly and on their merits, wherever they come from, so being able to ask a naive question without ego — and to disagree with someone senior without making it personal — matters more than seniority.
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

lists.content:
Understand what is possible, and turn it into requirements
  • Spend the bulk of your time with engineering: understanding architectures, constraints, and dependencies well enough to judge what is realistically doable in a given timeframe.
  • Translate strategic direction into clear requirements and use cases that engineering can act on directly, and follow them down to the Jira tickets.
  • Surface and shape the good ideas that come from engineering — many of the best ones do — and connect them to a product rationale.
  • Define success criteria for each capability, and verify they are actually met through implementation and delivery.
  • Maintain an accurate, shared view of Loft's product capabilities, what is in development, and where the gaps are.

    • Bring the outside in

    • Run customer discovery interviews alongside business development, and debrief missions to see how Loft's capabilities are actually used in operations.
    • Engage directly with the partners building on our platform, including the onboard AI application ecosystem, to understand their needs and constraints.
    • Track market trends and competitive moves closely enough to know where our offering stands.

      • Decide and prioritize

      • Own the roadmap for your perimeter, reconciling customer needs, engineering reality, and Loft's strategy into a single coherent plan.
      • Build the analysis behind every recommendation — sizing, segmentation, business cases, operational data — so decisions are grounded in evidence rather than intuition alone.
      • Negotiate scope and delivery commitments with engineering leadership, and re-plan when capacity or mission timelines shift.
      • Challenge, constructively and with data, business development, engineering leadership, and your own assumptions.

        • Communicate

        • Own internal communication on your perimeter: keep engineering, program leadership, and executives working from the same technical reality.
        • Develop the technical narratives and proof points that marketing and BD then turn into their own customer-facing material.
        • Prepare recommendations and presentations for top-executive-level audiences.

• 7+ years of professional experience, including hands-on product management.
  • Domain experience in at least one of: earth observation, embedded systems, aerospace systems, security & defense.
  • Comfort at both ends of the spectrum — understand the market, and the technology
  • Structured and data-driven: you bring your experience and your intuitions, but when you put a recommendation on the table you can show the analysis it stands on.
  • Real product obsession: you think about the bigger picture and product-market fit before you think about features.
  • Relentless curiosity. In a single month you might move from a satellite bus constraint, to onboard AI inference, to a defense accreditation requirement — and you need to find that stimulating rather than exhausting.
  • High autonomy and a bias for action: handed a broad perimeter, you organize it yourself and come back with a plan.
  • At ease being challenged, and challenging others, in a fast-moving and demanding environment.
  • Working knowledge of both hardware and software development lifecycles.
  • Proficient using and configuring Atlassian tools (Jira and Confluence).
  • Fluency in English, written and spoken.
  • Willingness to travel to other Loft offices and to customers.

• Fluency in French.
  • Experience with AI/ML products, edge computing, or developer and partner platforms and ecosystems.
  • Experience with satellite operations, constellation services, or ground segment products.
  • Exposure to institutional and defense customers and their procurement cycles.
  • Experience in a fast-growing, entrepreneurial NewSpace company or venture-backed deep-tech startup.
  • Professional experience working with international teams across time zones.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

lists.content:
Understand what is possible, and turn it into requirements
  • Spend the bulk of your time with engineering: understanding architectures, constraints, and dependencies well enough to judge what is realistically doable in a given timeframe.
  • Translate strategic direction into clear requirements and use cases that engineering can act on directly, and follow them down to the Jira tickets.
  • Surface and shape the good ideas that come from engineering — many of the best ones do — and connect them to a product rationale.
  • Define success criteria for each capability, and verify they are actually met through implementation and delivery.
  • Maintain an accurate, shared view of Loft's product capabilities, what is in development, and where the gaps are.

    • Bring the outside in

    • Run customer discovery interviews alongside business development, and debrief missions to see how Loft's capabilities are actually used in operations.
    • Engage directly with the partners building on our platform, including the onboard AI application ecosystem, to understand their needs and constraints.
    • Track market trends and competitive moves closely enough to know where our offering stands.

      • Decide and prioritize

      • Own the roadmap for your perimeter, reconciling customer needs, engineering reality, and Loft's strategy into a single coherent plan.
      • Build the analysis behind every recommendation — sizing, segmentation, business cases, operational data — so decisions are grounded in evidence rather than intuition alone.
      • Negotiate scope and delivery commitments with engineering leadership, and re-plan when capacity or mission timelines shift.
      • Challenge, constructively and with data, business development, engineering leadership, and your own assumptions.

        • Communicate

        • Own internal communication on your perimeter: keep engineering, program leadership, and executives working from the same technical reality.
        • Develop the technical narratives and proof points that marketing and BD then turn into their own customer-facing material.
        • Prepare recommendations and presentations for top-executive-level audiences.

• 7+ years of professional experience, including hands-on product management.
  • Domain experience in at least one of: earth observation, embedded systems, aerospace systems, security & defense.
  • Comfort at both ends of the spectrum — understand the market, and the technology
  • Structured and data-driven: you bring your experience and your intuitions, but when you put a recommendation on the table you can show the analysis it stands on.
  • Real product obsession: you think about the bigger picture and product-market fit before you think about features.
  • Relentless curiosity. In a single month you might move from a satellite bus constraint, to onboard AI inference, to a defense accreditation requirement — and you need to find that stimulating rather than exhausting.
  • High autonomy and a bias for action: handed a broad perimeter, you organize it yourself and come back with a plan.
  • At ease being challenged, and challenging others, in a fast-moving and demanding environment.
  • Working knowledge of both hardware and software development lifecycles.
  • Proficient using and configuring Atlassian tools (Jira and Confluence).
  • Fluency in English, written and spoken.
  • Willingness to travel to other Loft offices and to customers.

• Fluency in French.
  • Experience with AI/ML products, edge computing, or developer and partner platforms and ecosystems.
  • Experience with satellite operations, constellation services, or ground segment products.
  • Exposure to institutional and defense customers and their procurement cycles.
  • Experience in a fast-growing, entrepreneurial NewSpace company or venture-backed deep-tech startup.
  • Professional experience working with international teams across time zones.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

salaryDescription: State law requires us to tell you the base compensation range for this role, which is $160,000- $200,000 per year. This is determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.  The salary range for this role is intentionally wide as we evaluate individuals based on their unique experience and abilities to fit our needs. Most importantly, we are excited to meet you, and see if you are a great fit for our team. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

This is a role for someone who wants to go deep on technically complex problems that span the full stack. You will work across ground processing, customer-facing tooling, and interface definition — contributing to architecture decisions, maintaining requirements and ICDs, and helping ensure the offering evolves in a consistent and product-relevant way. You will collaborate closely with engineering, product, and operations teams across sites to turn technical ambiguity into clear frameworks for implementation.

description:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
As a Satellite Operations Software Engineer, you will be a key contributor to the development, automation, and operation of Orbitworks’ satellite programs.
 
This is a hand on satellite operations role combined with software development and systems engineering to ensure mission success from design to orbit.
 
You will work across the full stack software, hardware, and operational interfaces to deliver robust, scalable solutions that support satellite commissioning, nominal operations, and anomaly resolution.

lists.content:
• Understand and develop customer Concept of Operations (CONOPS) for operational planning and execution
  • Interface with customers prior to and during mission deployment
  • Create and maintain mission plans, schedules, operational procedures, and data workflows.
  • Execute satellite operations, including participating in the on-call rotation as Satellite Controller/Flight Director
  • Configure and set up tools for satellite mission operations, including Python procedures, Grafana dashboards for telemetry monitoring, and contribution to improvement and development of internal mission control software ‘Cockpit’
  • Assess & resolve in-orbit anomalies, and maintain overall satellite performance including adherence to all relevant SLAs
  • Develop automation for both ground and space-based operations, using Python, Lua, and CUE-based scripting
  • Support test campaigns with a ‘test-as-you-fly’ philosophy, by developing procedures and tools for both AIT and flight operations

• Experience interacting with and managing customers
  • Strong background in satellite operations and/or experience working with downstream EO imagery data products
  • Willingness to train as a Satellite Controller/Flight Director, including commissioning and on-call rotation
  • Proven software development or scripting experience, with strong automation skills
  • Proficiency in Python and Git
  • Pragmatic mindset with ability to balance short- and long-term operational goals
  • High accountability, autonomy, and ownership in delivering results
  • Openness to learning and working outside comfort zones in a fast-paced environment

• Strong understanding of the end-to-end satellite imagery value chain
  • Experience working with defence customers
  • Experience with Airbus satellite platforms (Arrow-150 bus) in Avionics, ADCS, or propulsion
  • Experience with LEO satellite operations and constellation management
  • Background in satellite testing, AIT, validation and verification of complex systems
  • Arabic language skills
  • Proficiency in Lua and CUE

lists.content:
• Serve as satellite systems engineer for one or more customer missions, representing Loft in technical discussions and reviews to accommodate and fly a variety of payloads
  • Act as the internal payload subject-matter expert, interfacing with hardware and software teams to ensure end-to-end integration.
  • Work with flight operations to develop the mission CONOPS, supporting the development of Service Level Agreements with Loft's customers
  • Assist with program management and product management, including interfacing with customers on programmatic and schedule matters
  • Review test plans and test results, and participate in the integration, test campaign, launch and in-orbit activities 
  • Accommodate customer missions on Loft’s rideshare programs, contributing to satellite-level budgets and analyses, V&V planning, CONOPS definition, AIT, and on-orbit operations.

• A minimum of 5 years of demonstrated experience as a spacecraft systems engineer, or equivalent experience in at least two different subsystems (ADCS, Mechanical, Thermal, Power, On-Board Electronics & Software, …)
  • You have strong communication and organizational skills
  • You challenge norms in aerospace engineering and testing activities and or experienced in fast-paced development environment
  • You have experience in small satellite assembly, integration and test campaigns, and/or in spacecraft delivery to orbit
  • You handle pressure positively and are always ready to put hands-on

• Experience with Python and Jupyter notebooks for analysis and simulation
  • Exposure to different space payload technologies (e.g., RF, optical, radar, hosted compute,…)
  • Exposure to in-orbit operations 
  • International experience

• Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success
  • Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best
  • Health and life insurance, we care about your health
  • Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand)
  • Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences
  • Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together
  • Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

• Strong proficiency in Python for backend engineering.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly, and work effectively across engineering, operations, and business teams.
  • Proactive problem-solving mindset, comfortable challenging assumptions constructively and taking ownership of features from design through production operations.

• Experience in the design, modeling, or analysis of space missions, with an understanding of mission lifecycle complexities.
  • Experience building customer-facing interfaces, customer portals, or platforms.
  • Experience designing or developing tasking interfaces or platforms, particularly in the satellite or Earth Observation domain.
  • Proficiency with Django and GraphQL, and familiarity with modern cloud infrastructure platforms (e.g. GCP/AWS, Kubernetes).

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
Loft Orbital is revolutionizing access to space by building reliable, shareable satellites that drastically reduce the time and complexity traditionally required to get to orbit. We operate satellites, fly customer payloads, and handle entire missions from end-to-end. We’re a close-knit team of space enthusiasts, software experts, and cutting-edge technologists, all working together to make space simple for our customers.
 
As a SeniorCloud Infrastructure Engineer on our Cloud Infrastructure Team, you’ll play a pivotal role in maintaining and scaling our ground segment infrastructure. You’ll collaborate across development, operations, and IT to ensure the integration, delivery, and reliability of services that support our space operations on Earth and in orbit.
 
This is an exciting opportunity to work on cutting-edge technology and help build modern automated space infrastructure. This is not your typical SRE role, we apply DevOps principles even to spacecraft control. Yes, we call it SatDevOps, and we’ll train you to operate our satellites!

Wanna join the adventure?
Are you passionate about optical payloads, image quality, and turning pixels into products customers can actually use? If so, this is the perfect role for you!
Loft flies multiple satellites per year and is building the next generation of Earth observation capability - from payload design through calibration, processing, and delivery - across a growing fleet of spacecraft. We're looking for a Senior Earth Observation Engineer to serve as the technical authority for optical payloads, image quality, and Earth observation mission performance across Loft.
This role requires expertise in imagery calibration, optical payloads, and image processing pipelines. You'll work closely with mission teams, customers, and payload suppliers to define performance requirements, drive payload development and test, support in-orbit calibration and commissioning, and ensure Loft can reliably process and deliver imagery to customers.
You'll help build the data processing and image-quality foundation that turns raw payload data into a sellable product, enabling Loft to simulate, calibrate, and deliver imagery across diverse customer missions and to leverage the AI boom through vision-based Earth observation.
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.
description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Are you passionate about optical payloads, image quality, and turning pixels into products customers can actually use? If so, this is the perfect role for you!

Loft flies multiple satellites per year and is building the next generation of Earth observation capability - from payload design through calibration, processing, and delivery - across a growing fleet of spacecraft. We're looking for a Senior Earth Observation Engineer to serve as the technical authority for optical payloads, image quality, and Earth observation mission performance across Loft.

This role requires expertise in imagery calibration, optical payloads, and image processing pipelines. You'll work closely with mission teams, customers, and payload suppliers to define performance requirements, drive payload development and test, support in-orbit calibration and commissioning, and ensure Loft can reliably process and deliver imagery to customers.

You'll help build the data processing and image-quality foundation that turns raw payload data into a sellable product, enabling Loft to simulate, calibrate, and deliver imagery across diverse customer missions and to leverage the AI boom through vision-based Earth observation.

We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

lists.content:
• Work with Earth observation customers to derive mission and payload requirements, along with verification techniques, and flow these down to software and hardware teams, including suppliers
  • Follow and drive optical payload suppliers' development and test activities
  • Develop, with the AIT and OPS teams, the on-ground and in-orbit test and calibration strategy
  • Develop the on-board and on-ground data processing strategy
  • Support the Lead Systems Engineer in mission CONOPS development
  • Support business development activities for optical payload customers and Earth observation virtual missions
  • Support test procedures and participate in integration, test campaigns, launch, and in-orbit commissioning
  • Contribute to and own the development of the company's Earth observation roadmap

• You have 5 or more years of demonstrated experience as a space systems engineer on earth observation missions
  • You are very familiar with image quality metrics and imagery calibration aspects (geometric, radiometric, spectral, etc.)
  • You have good experience in optical payloads
  • You have coded in Python for at least one year
  • You have strong communication and organizational skills
  • You challenge norms in aerospace engineering and testing activities, and/or have experience in a fast-paced development environment
  • You handle pressure positively and are always ready to put in the hands-on work

• Good knowledge of deep learning and artificial neural networks
  • Experience in optics and detector technologies
  • Experience in optical ground support equipment
  • Knowledge of ADCS and navigation/flight dynamics aspects
  • International experience

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks in office
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for birthing parent and 10 weeks for non-birthing parent
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

Who We Are

Loft: Space Made Simple. 

Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
Loft Orbital builds a space infrastructure providing a fast & simple path to orbit. Using different flight proven buses, we design, integrate and operate spacecraft to fly physical or virtual customer payloads. We handle entire missions end to end, significantly reducing the lead-time and risk of a traditional space mission.

As a Senior Product Systems Engineer at Loft, you will own the architecture of our overall offering — the layer that sits above any single implementation team and brings coherence across ground, space, software, and hardware. You will define how Loft's platform is structured, how capabilities are allocated across segments, and how customers, third-party software, and Loft's own stack interact.

This is not a role about executing within a defined system. It is about shaping the system itself— making cross-cutting architecture decisions, defining interfaces and requirements at the offering level, and ensuring the ground processing chain and customer-facing tooling evolve in a way that is coherent, reusable, and product-relevant. You will work closely with engineering, product, and operations teams across sites, and your work will directly influence how Loft's offering is built, exposed, and scaled.
 
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

lists.content:
• Help define the general architecture of Loft’s offering across ground and space
  • Support capability allocation across hardware, software, ground, flight, Loft-owned components, and external components
  • Ensure the ground processing chain is defined and evolved as a coherent part of the offering
  • Help shape ground software tools and interfaces as the main entry point for customers
  • Clarify the interaction model between OBSW, ground software, customer software, third-party software, and Loft’s stack
  • Help define, organize, and maintain requirements, interfaces, and architectural boundaries for offering-level topics
  • Coordinate architecture discussions and drive alignment between product intent, system architecture, and implementation realities across teams
  • Contribute to CONOPS, ICDs, architecture notes, trade studies, and related technical documentation
  • Help ensure solutions are reusable, scalable, and understandable rather than tailored only to one mission
  • Support architecture reviews and technical decision-making on cross-cutting topics

• Strong systems engineering background in complex technical products spanning software and hardware
  • Experience working at the boundary between architecture definition, requirements structuring, and engineering implementation
  • Ability to structure complex systems into clear capabilities, interfaces, requirements, and responsibilities
  • Strong understanding of software-heavy systems, including distributed components, APIs, processing chains, and integration patterns
  • Ability to coordinate cross-functional technical work across several teams without relying on direct authority
  • Strong communication and documentation skills, including the ability to turn technical ambiguity into a clear framework for decisions and execution
  • Sound engineering judgment on the right level of rigor, abstraction, and specification for a growing organization

• Experience with space systems, including ground segment tooling, onboard software, or customer-facing technical platforms
  • Experience defining integration models involving customer-owned or third-party software
  • Experience with architecture trade studies, capability allocation, and system-level interface management
  • Familiarity with CONOPS, ICDs, and other architecture or interface documentation methods
  • Experience with onboard data processing and cloud-based ground software
  • Experience in international and cross-site engineering collaboration

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks in office
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for birthing parent and 10 weeks for non-birthing parent
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

salaryDescription: State law requires us to tell you the base compensation range for this role, which is $160,000- $210,000 per year in Colorado. This is determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.  The salary range for this role is intentionally wide as we evaluate individuals based on their unique experience and abilities to fit our needs. Most importantly, we are excited to meet you, and see if you are a great fit for our team. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

descriptionBody:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
Loft Orbital builds a space infrastructure providing a fast & simple path to orbit. Using different flight proven buses, we design, integrate and operate spacecraft to fly physical or virtual customer payloads. We handle entire missions end to end, significantly reducing the lead-time and risk of a traditional space mission.

As a Senior Product Systems Engineer at Loft, you will own the architecture of our overall offering — the layer that sits above any single implementation team and brings coherence across ground, space, software, and hardware. You will define how Loft's platform is structured, how capabilities are allocated across segments, and how customers, third-party software, and Loft's own stack interact.

This is not a role about executing within a defined system. It is about shaping the system itself— making cross-cutting architecture decisions, defining interfaces and requirements at the offering level, and ensuring the ground processing chain and customer-facing tooling evolve in a way that is coherent, reusable, and product-relevant. You will work closely with engineering, product, and operations teams across sites, and your work will directly influence how Loft's offering is built, exposed, and scaled.
 
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

lists.content:
Project Engineering & Facility Development
  • Coordinate facility expansion, cleanroom construction, infrastructure upgrades and future modification projects from planning through commissioning and handover.
  • Review engineering drawings, technical specifications, material submittals and contractor proposals.
  • Coordinate civil, architectural, MEP, fire protection and specialist cleanroom works.
  • Monitor project schedules, budgets, contractor performance, construction quality and progress.
  • Support procurement, technical evaluations, cost assessments, variations and project documentation.
  • Coordinate testing, commissioning, inspections, defect rectification and final handover.
  • Ensure construction and modification activities are carried out safely without disrupting ongoing manufacturing operations.
    • Infrastructure & Authority Coordination
  • Coordinate HVAC, chilled-water, electrical, fire protection, compressed-air and other facility utility installations.
  • Review infrastructure requirements, system capacities and interfaces with existing facilities.
  • Liaise with TAQA, Abu Dhabi Civil Defence (ADCD), KEZAD and other relevant authorities for NOCs, utility connections, inspections and statutory approvals.
  • Coordinate planned shutdowns, utility modifications and safe restoration of affected systems.

  • Lead and coordinate day-to-day EHS activities across construction, maintenance and manufacturing operations.
  • Conduct workplace inspections, risk assessments, hazard identification and safety audits.
  • Monitor contractor safety, permit-to-work compliance and safe working practices.
  • Coordinate incident investigations, corrective actions and emergency preparedness activities.
  • Maintain EHS documentation, compliance records and statutory registers.
  • Support implementation and continual improvement of ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 management systems.
  • Coordinate safety training, awareness programs and regulatory compliance activities.

Essential Requirements
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil or a related engineering discipline.
  • 7–12 years of relevant experience in industrial construction, facility expansion or infrastructure projects.
  • Strong technical knowledge of MEP systems, building utilities and industrial infrastructure.
  • Proven experience in project execution, contractor coordination, scheduling, cost monitoring and commissioning.
  • Experience working within operational industrial or manufacturing facilities.
  • Practical experience coordinating with TAQA, Abu Dhabi Civil Defence, KEZAD and other UAE authorities.
  • Hands-on experience in EHS implementation, risk assessments, workplace safety and contractor safety management.
  • Proficiency in MS Project or equivalent scheduling software, Microsoft Excel and engineering drawing review.
  • Strong communication, problem-solving and coordination skills.
  • Valid UAE driving licence.

• Experience in cleanrooms, controlled environments or high-technology manufacturing facilities.
  • Experience in industrial projects within Abu Dhabi or KEZAD.
  • NEBOSH IGC or equivalent occupational safety qualification.
  • Familiarity with ISO 45001, ISO 14001 and ISO 14644 standards.
  • PMP or equivalent project management certification.

description:
Wanna join the adventure?

At Loft Orbital, we have just successfully launched multiple satellites that we fly and operate ourselves. With these satellites in orbit and a wave of exciting missions launching soon, we are scaling up quickly as a global company.

We are looking for a Test Infrastructure Engineer to join the team building and maintaining Loft’s test infrastructure internationally across our Golden, CO and Toulouse, France sites.

lists.content:
As a Test Infrastructure Engineer, you will primarily help design, develop, and deploy our test infrastructure and the tools for automating both our hardware and software testing, which will help us scale as a company.Sitting between the spacecraft and all the other teams, you will have a big impact in ensuring that every element of our satellite works without any bugs.We are looking for engineers with a product mindset, who have a good understanding of embedded systems, networking, data exchange protocols, and experience with setting up software infrastructures. Additionally, we are looking for someone who is:
  • Able to work independently with some guidance. People owning their work is important to us!
  • Able to wear multiple hats as needs arise. We are a small company disrupting an entire industry!
  • Not afraid to get out of their comfort zone to explore and learn. Technologies are evolving at rapid rates, and we must stay relevant!
    • Key responsibilities include:
    • Design, build, deploy, and maintain high-fidelity Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testbeds that emulate spacecraft systems, sensors, and communication links.
    • Design, build, deploy, and maintain Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) that interfaces with space vehicles under Assembly, Integration & Tests, allowing Validation and Verification of spacecrafts and their software before their launch campaigns.
    • Develop tools and frameworks that allow teams to simulate faults, edge cases, and mission scenarios that are difficult or costly to reproduce with physical hardware alone.
    • Work closely with systems, software, hardware, and operations teams to understand evolving test requirements and integrate feedback into the platforms.
    • Maintain and extend test infrastructure to support continuous integration (CI) pipelines, ensuring every code change is validated with realistic system-level tests.
    • Troubleshoot complex system issues spanning software, embedded hardware, networking, and system configuration.
      • Our culture at Loft Orbital promotes collaboration and ownership among our developers, fostering efforts hand in hand with other teams, internally and externally.

• 2+ years working with Linux systems, including configuration, debugging, and system-level troubleshooting.
  • Strong understanding of networking fundamentals (OSI layers, packet analysis, data exchange protocols like TCP/IP and UDP).
  • Hands-on experience with embedded systems or low-level hardware (Raspberry Pi, Arduino, microcontrollers, or similar).
  • Proficiency in Python (3.9+) for building test automation frameworks, device drivers, or test orchestration tools.
  • Experience containerizing applications with Docker.
  • Familiarity with at least one modern CI tool (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab CI, Buildkite, CircleCI) and integrating test pipelines.

• Experience designing or automating complex HIL/SIL testbed, signal conditioning, fault injection, or hardware emulation.
  • Experience with “Infrastructure-as-Code” systems, specifically NixOS.
  • Familiarity with networking simulation tools (e.g., network emulators, virtual switches) for testing data flows under realistic mission constraints.
  • Interest or experience with hardware test automation frameworks (e.g., custom Python-based test rigs).
  • Master’s degree in Computer Science or a similar field.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
 
As a Site Reliability Engineer with strong networking skills in our Cloud Infrastructure (SRE) team, you help the team own the networks that keep Loft running: cloud networking, VPN and site-to-site connectivity, segmentation, and routing across our offices, test equipment, and ground stations. You keep them reliable, observable, and secure as we scale. You coordinate with IT on the network components that interface with the physical infrastructure used by employees. You coordinate with the Test-Infrastructure team to ensure our test equipment is securely accessible.
You’ll work the way an SRE team works: defining reliability in measurable terms (SLOs for connectivity and ground-station availability), instrumenting the systems that prove it, managing the network as code, and automating away toil so on-call load doesn’t grow with the fleet.
Beyond the network, you’ll help the SRE team across its broader scope by participating in all the daily work just like a regular SRE: platform reliability and expansion, incident response, planning and user support.
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

You coordinate with the Test-Infrastructure team to ensure our test equipment is securely accessible.

You’ll work the way an SRE team works: defining reliability in measurable terms (SLOs for connectivity and ground-station availability), instrumenting the systems that prove it, managing the network as code, and automating away toil so on-call load doesn’t grow with the fleet.

Beyond the network, you’ll help the SRE team across its broader scope by participating in all the daily work just like a regular SRE: platform reliability and expansion, incident response, planning and user support.

lists.content:
• Participate in the design and implement Loft’s network architecture; cloud networking, VPN/site-to-site, segmentation, and routing across offices, ground stations, and test equipment
  • Tighten the network security posture: segmentation, access, and connectivity hardening
  • Manage the network as code: IaC provisioning, CI/CD, and GitOps
  • Define SLOs for connectivity and ground-station availability, and own the observability (metrics, logs, tracing) that measures them; Grafana-centric stacks a plus
  • Investigate and resolve reliability issues with root-cause analysis and durable fixes; reduce operational toil through automation
  • Contribute to the SRE team’s broader reliability and incident-response work, fostering the SatDevOps culture that power Loft’s DNA

• 4–5 years in network engineering, with deep hands-on networking: routing, VPN/site-to-site, segmentation, DNS, firewalling
  • Hands-on Software-Defined Networking: comfortable managing networks programmatically / as code rather than appliance-by-appliance (everything we run is IaC)
  • Strong public-cloud networking experience, ideally GCP (VPCs, peering, hybrid connectivity)
  • Comfortable operating on a Kuburnetes platform (k8s, Docker) and occasionally writing code
  • Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform or similar) and a CI/CD-driven, GitOps workflow
  • An SRE mindset: SLOs, observability, and reducing toil through automation
  • Ability to debug connectivity issues in a complex, hybrid network environment
  • Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

• Network certifications (CCNP or similar)
  • Hands-on experience with GitOps frameworks (ArgoCD, FluxCD)
  • Interest or experience in FinOps and cost-optimized architectures
  • Familiarity with security practices: vulnerability scanning, threat detection, risk mitigation
  • Understanding of orchestration in resource-constrained environments, like space systems

• Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success
  • Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best
  • Health and life insurance, we care about your health
  • Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand)
  • Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences
  • Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together
  • Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

description:
Wanna Join the Adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for a Mechanical Engineering Intern to join our team in Golden, Colorado for Summer 2027. You’ll work alongside our Mechanical Engineering team on the design and development of hardware for satellite missions.

This internship is designed to give you meaningful ownership of a real mechanical engineering project. You’ll gain hands-on experience taking a design from early requirements and concept development through detailed design, analysis, engineering documentation, and potentially prototyping.

lists.content:
As a Mechanical Engineering Intern, you’ll contribute to the design and development of a new mechanical subsystem or product that could ultimately support future Loft missions.

Depending on team priorities and active development work during the summer, you may:

  • Translate project needs into mechanical requirements and design constraints
  • Develop concepts and detailed 3D CAD models for satellite hardware
  • Perform structural analysis and support design validation
  • Create engineering drawings, including dimensions and tolerances
  • Coordinate with electrical, systems, manufacturing, and other engineering stakeholders
  • Support prototyping, manufacturing, and design iteration
  • Contribute to mechanical engineering standards, documentation, and best practices
  • Present your work and key learnings at the end of the internship

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field; undergraduate students must be rising juniors or rising seniors
  • Experience with CAD / 3D modeling through coursework, projects, research, or internships
  • Foundational understanding of mechanical design and analysis
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills
  • Curiosity, initiative, and interest in hands-on spacecraft hardware development

• Hands-on machining, manufacturing, or prototyping experience
  • Exposure to electronics packaging or mechanical design around electrical components
  • Experience participating in multidisciplinary engineering teams such as robotics, Formula SAE, rocketry, or CubeSat
  • Experience leading a school, club, or technical project
  • Previous internship, aerospace, or other relevant hands-on engineering experience

lists.text: During Your Internship, You Can Expect To
lists.content:
• Gain hands-on experience designing hardware that could support future satellite missions
  • Own meaningful engineering work from requirements through design and potentially prototyping
  • Receive ongoing mentorship and feedback from your mentor and manager
  • Work across engineering disciplines and learn how mechanical systems integrate into a spacecraft
  • Build relationships with fellow interns and Loft employees
  • Share your work and key learnings at the end of the internship

• Hourly compensation: $30.00/hour
  • Timing: Full-time, 10–12 week Summer 2027 internship. Start and end dates will be coordinated based on school schedule and team availability.
  • Location: On-site in Golden, Colorado
  • Relocation: Loft offers housing/relocation support for interns traveling from outside the local area.
  • In-office perks: Daily catered lunches and snacks

description:
Wanna Join the Adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for a Satellite Programs Intern to support technical program management across our satellite programs in Golden, Colorado for Summer 2027. You’ll work alongside our Satellite Programs team, helping turn customer and mission needs into executable satellite programs from early planning through launch and early orbit operations.

This internship sits at the intersection of engineering and business. You’ll work across technical disciplines, contribute to real program execution, and help improve the tools and processes our teams use to manage cost, schedule, risk, and technical scope.

lists.content:
As a Satellite Programs Intern, you’ll work alongside Satellite Program Managers and cross-functional engineering teams to support active programs while also owning meaningful work that helps strengthen how the team operates.

Depending on team priorities and active programs during the summer, you may:

  • Support the execution of a satellite program alongside a Satellite Program Manager
  • Build, refine, or maintain program schedules, including Integrated Master Schedules (IMS)
  • Develop or improve tools and processes used to track program risks, actions, and dependencies
  • Support cost tracking, forecasting, and program reporting activities
  • Help coordinate technical scope, priorities, and information across cross-functional teams
  • Own program management process-improvement projects across schedule, cost, risk, or technical scope
  • Analyze program data and translate findings into clear updates, recommendations, or next steps
  • Present your work and key learnings at the end of the internship

    • Projects may vary based on team priorities, but could include improving an Integrated Master Schedule template, building a program risk register and supporting risk reviews, or developing a bottoms-up cost estimate for an active satellite program.

description:
Wanna Join the Adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for a Thermal & Manufacturing Engineering Intern to join our team in Golden, Colorado for Summer 2027. You’ll work alongside our Mission Engineering & Analysis and Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) teams to improve how thermal interface materials are selected, prepared, and used in spacecraft assembly.

This internship offers hands-on experience at the intersection of materials, mechanical engineering, and manufacturing. You’ll work directly with AIT technicians and engineers, taking your work from CAD drawings to physical parts used on satellites. You’ll take a process improvement from initial experiments through validation and documentation, then see it used in spacecraft assembly.

lists.content:
As a Thermal & Manufacturing Engineering Intern, you’ll help develop and validate a workflow for preparing thermal interface materials, including gap pads, thermal tapes, and graphite sheets. These materials help transfer heat between spacecraft components, and their preparation requires attention to accuracy, cleanliness, and handling.

Depending on team priorities, you may:

  • Plan and conduct trials to compare materials and cutting methods, including laser cutting, digital knife cutting, and die-cutting
  • Evaluate cut quality, dimensional accuracy, material handling, and contamination risks
  • Develop a repeatable workflow from CAD drawings to cut parts and assembly-ready kits
  • Help establish drawing and DXF file conventions, document cutting settings, and define inspection steps
  • Develop approaches for labeling, protective liners, packaging, and handling to simplify assembly
  • Create work instructions and inspection checklists in collaboration with engineering and AIT teams
  • Present findings and recommend materials and processes that balance thermal requirements with practical manufacturing needs

• Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field; undergraduate students must be rising juniors or rising seniors
  • Proficiency with SolidWorks or equivalent CAD software and ability to create clear engineering drawings
  • Hands-on fabrication or test experience through projects, research, internships, or shop/lab work
  • Ability to plan structured experiments, record data, and analyze results using Python, Excel, or similar tools
  • Strong written communication skills, including documenting procedures and findings
  • Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a passion for space

• Familiarity with Python scripting
  • Foundational knowledge of heat transfer and thermal principles
  • Awareness of cleanroom practices, electrostatic discharge (ESD), and contamination control
  • Exposure to spaceflight hardware through coursework, research, projects, or internships

description:
Role overview

Build local suppliers’ capability to manufacture flight hardware for Orbitworks. This new role combines manufacturing engineering, supplier quality and hands-on process development, with an initial focus on machined components, wire harness assemblies and structural honeycomb panel rework or modifications.

The SDM will assess suppliers on site, close manufacturing process gaps and establish repeatable qualification and development methods. The role starts as an individual contributor, working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Procurement, Contracts and D2M, with potential to build a broader supplier development function over time.

lists.content:
• Assess supplier manufacturing readiness through on-site process audits, capability reviews and risk assessments.
  • Work with suppliers to improve travelers, work instructions, inspection plans and process controls, including torque control, crimp validation and bonding where applicable.
  • Validate machining capability, including CNC programming discipline, tooling, GD&T interpretation, surface finish, material traceability and first article inspection.
  • Strengthen wire harness production through crimp and pull-test validation, routing and shielding controls, workmanship standards and manufacturing records.
  • Oversee honeycomb panel rework and modifications, ensuring bonding validation, environmental controls, configuration integrity and alignment with nondestructive inspection requirements.
  • Implement AS9100-aligned practices, AS9102 first article inspection, APQP and PPAP where applicable.
  • Lead containment, root cause analysis and corrective action for supplier quality escapes.
  • Develop supplier development roadmaps, qualification criteria and performance dashboards covering quality, delivery, FAI results, escapes and process capability.
  • Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality and Supply Chain to resolve technical issues and align supplier readiness with flight requirements.

• Flight-hardware manufacturing experience with a clear understanding of aerospace process control, documentation and traceability requirements.
  • Deep machining knowledge covering CNC processes, GD&T, materials, tooling, surface finish and inspection.
  • Wire harness manufacturing expertise, including crimp validation, pull testing, routing, shielding and workmanship controls.
  • Proven supplier development experience with measurable improvements in capability, quality or manufacturing readiness.
  • Working knowledge of AS9100-based quality systems, AS9102 first article inspection and manufacturing process validation.
  • Experience leading root cause analysis, containment and corrective action using methods such as 8D or RCCA.
  • Hands-on shop-floor expertise, the ability to work independently and strong communication skills to align suppliers with internal technical stakeholders.

• Honeycomb or composite structures, bonding, nondestructive inspection and controlled structural rework experience.
  • IPC/WHMA-A-620 certification or knowledge of certification requirements; NADCAP special process exposure.
  • Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), Lean or Six Sigma Black Belt experience.
  • Experience building a supplier development function, integrating ERP/MRP systems or working with international suppliers.

description:
Role Overview

Orbitworks is looking for an experienced supplier management professional to lead the tactical execution of supplier management across our UAE and international supply base, including our internal supply relationship with Loft Orbital Solutions.

This role combines technical procurement expertise, commercial ownership, and hands-on execution to keep conforming hardware, equipment, and services arriving on time and at a competitive total cost. You'll own the full supplier lifecycle — from quotations, sourcing, and purchase orders through onboarding, delivery, performance management, renewal, and offboarding.

Sitting within the Supply Chain team, you'll partner closely with Engineering, Quality, Planning, Programs, Finance, and our Supplier Development function. This is an individual-contributor role with real strategic weight: you'll build the processes and working relationships needed to support a fast-growing portfolio of technologies and flight hardware.

lists.content:
• Own the supplier portfolio — Manage a mix of local and international suppliers alongside internal supply partners, segmenting them by criticality, technology, capacity, lead time, and risk, and setting the right level of ownership and review cadence for each.
  • Lead technical sourcing and quotations — Turn approved specifications, drawings, and documentation requirements into effective RFQs, then evaluate quotes with Engineering and QA on compliance, lead time, capacity, tooling costs, and total cost of ownership.
  • Drive procurement execution — Own requisitions, PO placement and amendments, supplier acknowledgement, and delivery follow-up, keeping quantities, prices, and delivery dates accurate and resolving receipt or invoice discrepancies.
  • Negotiate contracts and commercial terms — Negotiate and administer pricing, payment, delivery, warranty, change, cancellation, and tooling-ownership terms with Legal and Compliance, ensuring quality and technical requirements flow through into every order.
  • Manage demand and product availability — Connect production and program demand to supplier lead times and capacity, flag shortages and long-lead exposure early, and secure the coverage needed while managing cash and obsolescence risk.
  • Lead delivery recovery — Validate supplier milestones and delivery evidence, and run recovery plans and escalations through to verified closure when things go off track.
  • Manage the supplier lifecycle — Coordinate due diligence, onboarding, qualification, approved status, and offboarding, protecting continuity of orders, tooling, and records during transitions.
  • Partner on quality and technical issues — Work with QA on supplier nonconformances and corrective actions, coordinate technical changes with Engineering, and turn Supplier Development findings into sourcing and commercial decisions.
  • Run Loft Orbital and internal supply execution — Establish clear demand handoffs, commitments, and escalation paths with Loft counterparts, and apply consistent expectations across internal supply relationships.
  • Improve performance and cost — Run supplier reviews on delivery, quality, responsiveness, and risk, and improve total cost through negotiation, order strategy, and qualified alternatives.
  • Build the function — Create practical processes, dashboards, and decision records, and coach procurement colleagues as the portfolio and team grow.

    •

• 7–15 years of experience in supplier management, technical procurement, or supply chain within aerospace, space, or another demanding engineered-product environment, with direct accountability for production hardware or technically complex supply.
  • Technical procurement literacy — able to read specifications, drawings, BOMs, revisions, and acceptance requirements, and knows when Engineering or QA sign-off is required.
  • Hands-on, end-to-end procurement experience, including RFQs, quotation comparisons, approvals, POs, amendments, delivery follow-up, and supplier lifecycle management.
  • Demonstrated commercial and contract depth, with the ability to speak to specific terms you've personally negotiated and the risks they addressed.
  • A track record of preventing or resolving shortages, managing capacity or long-lead constraints, and restoring supplier commitments with measurable results.
  • Experience owning a supplier portfolio: segmenting risk, running performance reviews, and driving corrective actions to closure.
  • Strong cross-functional influence across Procurement, Engineering, QA, Planning, Finance, and suppliers, including relationships without direct authority.
  • Comfort working in ERP/MRP systems and connecting demand, supply, lead times, and PO data to assess cost, inventory, and cash impact.
  • Experience building processes and coaching colleagues in a fast-growing, still-forming environment.
  • A degree in engineering, supply chain, or a related field (or equivalent demonstrated experience), with clear professional English communication; Arabic and French are a plus.

• Experience with space or aerospace flight hardware, including traceability, configuration, qualification, and controlled-change requirements.
  • Background in complex electronics, avionics, harnesses, precision machining, structures, propulsion, or optical payloads.
  • UAE or regional supplier experience.
  • Experience managing intercompany or joint-venture supply relationships.
  • Experience supporting new product introduction and the transition from development to production-scale purchasing.
  • Familiarity with supplier development and quality systems; AS9100 or equivalent experience is a plus.
  • A professional certification such as CIPS, CPSM, or CSCP, plus cost-breakdown or should-cost experience.
  • Familiarity with international logistics, customs, and export-control considerations.

Orbitworks is building satellite systems and space operations capability out of the UAE, working in close partnership with Loft Orbital Solutions. As we scale our technology portfolio, this role sits at the center of making sure the hardware, equipment, and services behind our programs show up on time, at the right quality, and at the right cost.

description:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is revolutionizing access to space by building reliable, shareable satellites that drastically reduce the time and complexity traditionally required to get to orbit. We operate satellites, fly customer payloads, and handle entire missions from end-to-end. We’re a close-knit team of space enthusiasts, software experts, and cutting-edge technologists, all working together to make space simple for our customers.

As a passionate and experienced Team Lead for our Cloud Infrastructure Team, you will play a mission-critical leadership role, you will oversee a dynamic group of cloud engineers responsible for building and maintaining the cloud-based ground segment that powers our rapidly expanding constellation of satellites.
You will set the technical direction, foster collaboration across teams, champion DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) best practices, and directly contribute to our mission of making access to space fast, simple, and reliable.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who thrives in high-growth environments, enjoys technical challenges at scale, and is passionate about mentorship, reliability, and innovation.

lists.content:
• Lead, mentor, and grow a team of highly skilled cloud infrastructure engineers.
  • Own and run daily team operations, including standups, sprint planning, retrospectives, and sync meetings to ensure clear priorities, high execution velocity, and smooth communication.
  • Foster a culture of technical excellence, continuous learning, psychological safety, and collaborative problem-solving.
  • Define and communicate the team's mission, vision, and goals aligned with Loft Orbital’s broader business objectives.
  • Champion a DevOps/SRE mindset across the company, promoting ownership of reliability, scalability, and security.
  • Set and drive the cloud infrastructure strategy, ensuring systems are secure, scalable, and cost-effective.

descriptionPlain:
Wanna join the adventure?
Loft Orbital's mission is to make space simple. We deploy customer missions on our satellite infrastructure so our customers can focus on their applications instead of the spacecraft underneath them. The Customer Delivery team turns signed contracts into working missions on orbit and supports our customers from start to finish.
As a Technical Program Manager, Customer Delivery, you maintain the engine that drives the Customer Delivery team forward. You connect Loft's product development efforts to our customer value stream, ensuring the team has the right capabilities, tools, and plans to execute customer missions. You will work alongside our Customer Delivery Engineers (CDEs), who design and execute each customer mission, by building the development plans and capability portfolio they draw on to deliver value to our customers. You will own Mission Development Plans that coordinate work across engineering, product, and operations teams; manage the Customer Offering Portfolio that defines what Loft can deliver; and drive quality, visibility, and consistency in how new capabilities are deployed to our customer offering. This role is well suited to someone who has taken products from development through deployment at a product-driven technology company and wants to apply that discipline iteratively across an active product line of missions flying in orbit.

lists.content:
• Own the Mission Development Plan for assigned missions: identify all work required to deploy and execute the mission, break it down into committed work packages with contributing teams, and drive it to completion against launch-anchored deadlines
  • Manage the Customer Offering Portfolio: maintain the catalog of capabilities Loft can draw on to execute customer missions, identify deltas between the portfolio and upcoming mission needs, and drive new capability development with product and engineering teams
  • Partner with Customer Delivery Engineers to deliver customer value: CDEs execute the mission with the customer, and you ensure the capabilities, plans, and tooling they need are in place when they need them
  • Connect Customer Delivery to Loft's product organization by representing operational and customer constraints in product planning, and by managing the deployment of new features and capabilities into operational use
  • Drive cross-functional coordination and status clarity: run internal reviews with CDEs, report on development progress, risks, and blockers, and keep leadership and customers aligned on where things stand
  • Engage directly with customers, up to the executive level, on mission development scope, schedule, and capability tradeoffs
  • Continuously improve Customer Delivery processes, templates, and workflows to increase execution efficiency without sacrificing quality

• ~8 years of professional experience in technical program, product, or engineering roles
  • ~3 years as an Engineering Program Manager (EPM) or Product-focused Technical Program Manager (TPM) at a product-driven technology company, leading cross-functional programs from definition through ship
  • Experience deploying products into production or operational environments, including release readiness, cross-team dependency management, and post-deployment quality
  • Experience in the satellite or aerospace industry, with working knowledge of spacecraft systems, mission operations, or payload development
  • Experience working directly with external customers, including executive-level stakeholders
  • Exceptional and proven technical aptitude: able to go deep with engineers on architecture and tradeoffs, and translate that fluently for customers and executives
  • Excellent communication skills at all levels, from engineering deep dives to executive summaries, with the organization and prioritization skills to run multiple parallel workstreams in a fast-paced environment

• Direct experience with satellite on-orbit operations, commissioning, or ground segment software
  • Technical leadership experience (leading engineers or technical teams, formally or informally)
  • Experience building or managing a product/capability portfolio, roadmap, or plan of record
  • Experience with international customers and distributed teams

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks in office
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for birthing parent and 10 weeks for non-birthing parent
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

description:
Wanna join the adventure?

We’re looking for a Technical Recruiter with a strong background in hardware and product engineering recruitment who is excited to help Loft Orbital scale its satellite engineering and production teams. In this role, you’ll own the full-cycle recruiting process—from sourcing to offer—for highly specialized hardware engineering positions critical to the design, development, integration, and operation of our satellite systems. You’ll partner closely with hiring managers to identify and attract top talent across mechanical engineering, electrical and electronics engineering, embedded systems, RF, systems engineering, and hardware test.
 
We’re hiring for one position across multiple locations - you only need to apply once.

lists.content:
• 3+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting experience, with a strong focus on hardware and engineering roles, ideally in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Demonstrated strength in proactive sourcing, including LinkedIn Recruiter, advanced Boolean search techniques, and creative approaches to identifying and engaging passive candidates.
  • Experience recruiting technical talent across hardware and product engineering disciplines, including mechanical engineering, electrical/electronics, embedded systems, firmware, RF/wireless, systems engineering, and hardware test.
  • Strong understanding of hardware engineering concepts and technologies, including CAD, GD&T, PCB design, signal integrity, power electronics, and complex electromechanical systems.
  • Ability to understand and translate highly technical requirements into effective sourcing strategies, including specialized areas such as embedded C/C++, RTOS, microcontrollers, FPGA, RF systems, antennas, and EMI/EMC.
  • Familiarity with engineering verification and validation processes, hardware test methodologies, and environmental testing.
  • Experience recruiting within aerospace, space, satellite, defense, or adjacent complex hardware/deep-tech industries.
  • Proven ability to build and maintain strong talent pipelines for specialized hardware engineering positions in competitive markets.
  • Ability to effectively pitch Loft’s mission, culture, and technical challenges to highly specialized, passive candidates.
  • Experience conducting phone screens, assessing technical alignment, and managing candidate communication throughout the full interview lifecycle.
  • Proficiency with ATS tools (Lever preferred), including maintaining accurate and up-to-date pipelines.
  • Collaborative mindset and ability to partner closely with hiring managers and the internal recruiting team, providing market insights and recommendations to improve hiring outcomes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Direct experience recruiting for satellite systems, avionics, GNC, RF engineering, hardware test, or assembly, integration, and test (AI&T) positions.
  • Familiarity with spacecraft hardware development, electronics manufacturing, PCB design, and satellite production environments.
  • Experience recruiting globally, with knowledge of both US and European aerospace and hardware engineering talent ecosystems.
  • Familiarity with ITAR, EAR, and compliance considerations relevant to US-based space and defense hiring.
  • Prior work in or close partnership with startup or high-growth aerospace companies.
  • Background in agency recruiting or experience managing multiple specialized technical searches simultaneously.
  • Skilled at using social platforms like LinkedIn to enhance employer brand and attract niche technical talent.
  • Comfort reporting on recruiting metrics, pipeline health, and sourcing performance.

• 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance option for employees and dependents
  • Flexible Spending (FSA) and Health Savings (HSA) Accounts offered with an employer contribution to the HSA
  • 100% employer paid Life, AD&D, Short-Term, and Long-Term Disability insurance
  • Flexible Time Off policy for vacation and sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • 401(k) plan and equity options
  • Daily catered lunches and snacks
  • International exposure to our team in France
  • Fully paid parental leave; 14 weeks for primary caregiver and 10 weeks for secondary caregiver
  • Carrot Fertility provides comprehensive, inclusive fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits with financial support
  • Off-sites and many social events and celebrations
  • Relocation assistance when applicable

salaryDescription: State law requires us to tell you the base compensation range for this role, which is $120,000- $150,000 per year. This is determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.  The salary range for this role is intentionally wide as we evaluate individuals based on their unique experience and abilities to fit our needs. Most importantly, we are excited to meet you, and see if you are a great fit for our team. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

In this remote role, you’ll focus on proactively identifying, engaging, and building pipelines of highly specialized engineering talent for some of our most challenging positions. You’ll work closely with our recruiters and hiring managers to develop targeted sourcing strategies, map competitive talent markets, and connect with exceptional passive candidates across hardware engineering disciplines.

lists.content:
• 3+ years of technical sourcing or recruiting experience, with a strong focus on hardware and engineering talent.
  • Demonstrated expertise in proactive headhunting, including LinkedIn Recruiter, advanced Boolean search, talent mapping, and creative sourcing techniques to identify hard-to-find candidates.
  • Experience sourcing technical talent across hardware engineering disciplines, including mechanical engineering, electrical/electronics, embedded systems, firmware, RF/wireless, systems engineering, and hardware test.
  • Strong understanding of hardware engineering concepts and terminology, including CAD, PCB design, embedded systems, microcontrollers, FPGA, RF systems, and hardware verification and validation.
  • Proven ability to identify and engage passive candidates for niche, highly specialized engineering positions.
  • Experience conducting initial candidate outreach, generating interest, and evaluating basic technical alignment before handing candidates over to recruiters.
  • Ability to independently develop sourcing strategies, identify target companies, and build talent pipelines for multiple technical requisitions.
  • Strong research and market-mapping skills, with the ability to identify relevant companies, emerging talent pools, and competitive hiring markets.
  • Ability to effectively pitch Loft’s mission, culture, and technical challenges to highly specialized, passive candidates.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple sourcing priorities while maintaining accurate candidate records and pipeline activity.
  • Proficiency with LinkedIn Recruiter and ATS tools (Lever preferred), including maintaining accurate sourcing pipelines and tracking outreach activity.
  • Collaborative mindset and ability to work closely with recruiters and hiring managers, providing sourcing insights, market intelligence, and candidate recommendations.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work independently in a remote environment.

• Direct experience sourcing talent within the space, satellite, aerospace, defense, or adjacent complex hardware/deep-tech industries.
  • Experience sourcing for specialized profiles such as avionics, GNC, RF engineering, PCB/board design, manufacturing engineering, or assembly, integration, and test (AI&T).
  • Prior experience as a dedicated technical sourcer, research specialist, or sourcing partner within an in-house recruiting team or agency.
  • Experience supporting high-volume sourcing initiatives or rapid engineering team expansion.
  • Knowledge of US and European aerospace and hardware engineering talent ecosystems, including key companies, startups, and talent hubs.
  • Familiarity with ITAR, EAR, and compliance considerations relevant to US-based space and defense hiring.
  • Experience using sourcing analytics to track outreach effectiveness, candidate engagement, and pipeline conversion.
  • Prior experience supporting startup or high-growth technical organizations.

We’re looking for a Technical Sourcer with a strong background in hardware and engineering talent identification to support Loft Orbital’s growing hiring needs on a six-month contract, with the possibility of extension. In this remote role, you’ll focus on proactively identifying, engaging, and building pipelines of highly specialized engineering talent for some of our most challenging positions. You’ll work closely with our recruiters and hiring managers to develop targeted sourcing strategies, map competitive talent markets, and connect with exceptional passive candidates across hardware engineering disciplines.

Who We Are

Loft: Space Made Simple. 

Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.

With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.

As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.
